When they stepped closer, the corpse stirred. What followed was battle in the dark. Yin Shen’s blades flashed in starlight. Hobbins darted between the giant’s ribs, hurling bursts of fire from Aronious’s bow. The creature tore free one arm, swinging its axe like a falling tree. Aronious’s thorn whip lashed around the haft, binding it fast. The ferret hurled her last vial of ink, blotting out one of the giant’s glowing eyes; Yin Shen followed, leaping to its skull and forcing a waterskin into the other. With a final, soul-shaking howl, the light died. The bones cracked, crumbled, and fell. A streak of blue fire shot from the ruin, vanishing through the cave mouth and into the storm beyond. When the echoes faded, the heroes stood alone in the stillness — three figures in the dark, their breath misting in victory and awe.
docs.title: Session 4: The Giant Beneath the Ice

docs.text: Session 5: Granny Maud and the Frozen Eye Flush with victory after felling the giant beneath the ice, the party lingered only long enough to steady their breath and share a brief, hard-earned celebration. Then they pressed onward, crossing the chamber toward the far exit — a narrow tunnel carved by time and frost. The passage split in two. From the right came a low, droning hum that vibrated through the stone. With a wary glance between them, the group chose the opposite path. The tunnel soon opened onto the same frozen river they had traversed before, though now they stood far downstream, where the ice ran smoother and deeper. Before stepping onto the glassy surface, they combed the frost-lined corridor for danger. It was Hobbins whose keen eyes caught what lay beneath — four massive giant skeletons suspended in perfect, crystalline ice. Their empty sockets flickered with the first sparks of cold blue flame. Yet the ice was flawless, a single unbroken sheet. The dead were trapped fast, unable to break free. Reassured, the party ventured out across the river. The humming returned — louder this time, now unmistakably from the right. Curiosity tugged at their steps, drawing them toward a gravelly shore. There, in the dim light, stood an elderly woman, pallid and gray as drift-frost. She hummed as she worked, her rusty cleaver rising and falling with a dull, wet rhythm against a cutting board. Before her lay a mound of mangled flesh — organs, meat, and bone sorted into grotesque piles. Behind her, a cauldron bubbled with some thick and foul concoction. She turned, lips peeling into a sneer. “Ahh, visitors,” she rasped. “Let Granny Maud prepare you some dinner.” She advanced. Aronious’s bow came up in an instant. Hobbins hurled spells across the beach, and Yin Shen swept in from the shadows. Their assault struck hard and fast. Under their combined force the old woman’s form split apart like shedding skin. What emerged was no mortal crone — but a towering, blue-skinned sea hag, her features twisted and wild with hunger. The sight hit Hobbins like a blow. Terror surged through her, freezing her steps and hollowing her breath. But Aronious and Yin Shen pressed the attack, breaking the hag’s spell with sheer ferocity. The battle was brutal but brief. At last the creature collapsed, her body sagging into the gravel. From her shriveled hand rolled a small orb glimmering blue in the dim cave light. All three reached for it at once. Only Hobbins closed her paw around it — smooth, cold, and humming with unnatural stillness. Not a trinket. Not a stone. But the frozen eye of a sea hag. The cavern fell quiet around them as its faint, icy glow pulsed in her grasp.

docs.title: Session 5: Granny Maud and the Frozen Eye

docs.text: Session 6: The Touch of Divinity With Granny Maud slain and her frozen eye safely pocketed by Hobbins , the party paused to consider their next move. Yin Shen , ever practical, drew her blade and severed the hag's head — proof enough for the folk of Easthaven that the killer of their fishermen was no more. The cavern stretched before them, its secrets still half-hidden in shadow. Hobbins' keen eyes fixed on an arched stone bridge high above the frozen river they had crossed before. Curiosity burned bright, and she was not one to leave mysteries unsolved. What followed was a spectacle both ridiculous and oddly effective. After a brief — and surprisingly technical — debate on the aerodynamics of a ferret in flight, Yin Shen's patience ran dry. With a sharp exhale and no ceremony whatsoever, she balled Hobbins up and hurled her skyward with all her strength. The ferret unfurled mid-arc, tumbling through the frigid air before landing in a pile of frost atop the bridge. Safe. Mostly dignified. Aronious turned to Yin Shen with a grin. Before she could protest, he seized her by the ankles and began to spin — once, twice, building momentum like a hammer throw. When he let go, Yin Shen sailed through the air... only to fall short of the mark. She thudded against the stone wall and crumpled to the cavern floor below. They decided to just climb. By the time Aronious and Yin Shen hauled themselves onto the bridge, Hobbins had already scurried off to explore its far end. There she found the remnants of an old campsite — a torn bedroll, cold ash from a long-dead fire, and scraps of paper covered in hasty scribbles. Nothing more. She reported her findings when the others arrived, and together they pressed onward, following the sound of gusting wind deeper into the mountain. The tunnel led them to a chamber lined floor-to-ceiling with ancient stone pillars. Along the walls, painted in faded pigment and frost-worn detail, were images of beasts — wolves, bears, eagles, and others — uncommonly large and surrounded by smaller kin. Each great creature bore a collar or band around its neck, and was haloed in blue light. Hobbins studied the paintings intently, whiskers twitching with thought, but could glean no further meaning. With a reluctant sigh, she rejoined the others, and the party moved on toward the exit. Outside, the wind tore at their cloaks and the sky hung gray and heavy with snow. They remembered then the final cave entrance — the one they had yet to investigate. It sat high on the cliffside, accessible only by a narrow ledge slick with ice. Hobbins scurried across easily, her small form unbothered by the drop below. She turned to watch the others follow. Aronious grinned. With a flick of his wrist, a thorned vine shot from his hand and coiled tight around an outcrop above. Before Yin Shen could object, he grabbed her by the arm and swung them both across the gap. Yin Shen's feet found purchase on the ice, but Aronious slipped. In a flash, she seized him by the shirt and yanked him back from the edge. The three of them stood together, breath misting in the cold, when a sound echoed from within the cave — low growling, threaded with whimpering pain. Hobbins crept forward, silent as shadow, and peered into the darkness. What she saw stopped her heart. A wolf. No — a dire wolf , but monstrous even by those standards. Twice the size of any she had ever seen, its bulk filled the cave like a mountain of fur and sinew. Its flanks were torn open, deep gashes still oozing red into matted gray fur. It licked at its wounds with slow, labored effort, eyes half-closed in exhaustion. Faint blue whisps could be seen rising from its form. Hobbins returned to the others and relayed what she had seen. After a brief, whispered debate, they agreed on a plan: Hobbins would disguise herself as a direwolf pup and attempt to communicate. She wove the magic carefully — first the transformation, her body rippling into the shape of a small wolf, then the spell of comprehension. On four legs, she padded into the cave. The great wolf's head lifted. His icy blue eyes fixed on her, wary but not hostile. Hobbins could not speak in words, but she could feel — impressions, emotions, intent. She sent warmth, safety, the desire to help. The wolf considered her for a long moment, then lowered his head in permission. The party entered. Hobbins set to work with her medicine kit, wrapping wounds, applying balm, stitching torn flesh with steady paws. Aronious knelt beside the beast and spoke the words of an old magic — Speak with Animals — and at last, understanding bloomed between them. The wolf's voice was deep and weary, but tinged with ancient pride. "I am Lupine ," he said. "Once a dire wolf. Now... something more." "I have quarreled with another of my kind." Aronious offered their services to hunt this adversary. Lupine's eyes flared with something close to panic. "No," he growled. "Do not seek her out alone. She is far beyond you." He told them he was an awakened godling — a creature granted intelligence, power, and a domain of his own. But his strength had been tested. Ursa, a polar bear godling, had grown discontent with the borders of her realm. She had attacked him, seeking to consume his domain and claim his power for herself. The fight had nearly killed him. Aronious asked if there was another way to help. Lupine's gaze softened. "There is," he said quietly. "Southeast of Easthaven lies a cave — small, cursed, and ruled by madness. Within it dwells Skree, an awakened bat. He is... unstable. Violent. A danger to all who wander near. His chaos threatens the balance we godlings keep. Deal with him, and you will have proven yourselves." He paused, then added with a rumble like distant thunder, "Skree is a deranged godling. Ursa is merely an ambitious cub. One must fall before the other can be faced." Before they left, Hobbins returned to her natural form and padded back to Lupine's side. She looked up at the great wolf, her small voice steady and sincere. "When you are healed," she said, "will you join us?" Lupine's amber eyes glinted with something that might have been respect. "Prove yourselves," he said, "and you will have an ally." The party stepped back into the winter cold, the wind biting at their faces and the snow swirling thick around them. Behind them, the cave fell silent once more. Ahead, the lights of Easthaven flickered faintly through the storm. And somewhere to the southeast, in a cave bound by madness and shadow, a bat-god waited.

docs.title: Session 6: The Touch of Divinity

docs.text: Session 7: The Gnome's Gambit and the Spider's Den The morning after their harrowing encounter with Lupine found the party seeking respite at The White Lady Inn . The innkeeper, recognizing them from their previous stay, offered a generous discount — one silver rather than the usual five — a small kindness in a land that offered few. While Yin Shen retreated to their room to nurse her wounds and gather her strength, Hobbins enlisted Aronious for a task both peculiar and demanding. Without explanation, she led him back across the frozen expanse of Lac Dinneshere . There, beneath the gray and endless sky, Hobbins commanded him to cut through the ice. For an hour, Aronious swung his blade, each strike sending chips and frost flying, until at last he broke through four feet of frozen lake. Before he could catch his breath, Hobbins launched herself toward the opening, the Sea Hag's Frozen Eye clutched in her outstretched paw. Aronious caught her mid-leap, stopping her just an inch above the black water below. "Don't move a muscle," Hobbins squeaked through chattering teeth, "for one hour." And so Aronious stood, bent double over the hole, muscles screaming in protest, while Hobbins plunged her tiny paws into the frigid depths. The eye turned and shifted beneath the surface, as if searching, seeking, seeing . The ferret's digits turned blue with cold, her body trembling with exhaustion, but she did not yield. At last, the eye went still. The cloudiness returned to its cornea, and understanding flooded through her. She had attuned. Aronious straightened slowly, every joint and sinew crying out in relief. Together, they returned to the inn. Rested and resolved, the party agreed their next task was clear: they would hunt Skree , the deranged bat godling whose madness threatened the fragile balance of the awakened. Yin Shen said nothing, but her mind was already turning. Without a word, she rose and strode into the streets of Easthaven . Hobbins and Aronious exchanged a glance, shrugged, and followed. The fox-spirited rogue led them down a narrow alley to a modest storefront: Strings and Sundries , a shop of wood and string instruments. Inside, a gnome with a bright red shirt greeted them cheerfully. His name, he said, was Finkle Shortfuse . Yin Shen asked for cymbals. Finkle apologized profusely but assured her that his cousin down the road would have exactly what she needed. He handed her a coupon — a scrap of old newspaper with the words "ONE DISCOWNT" scrawled in crooked letters. The party walked to the neighboring shop: Drums Emporium . As they entered, a commotion sounded from the back room, and out stepped an identical gnome — save for the blue shirt he wore. His name, he claimed, was Hansel Wiresnap . Hobbins' whiskers twitched. What followed was a comedy of suspicion and investigation. The party moved between the two shops, watching the "cousins" vanish into back rooms and reappear moments later in different colored shirts. During the commotion of moving between stores and multiple conversations, Hobbins and Yin Shen swiped cymbals and a violin from the store shelves. At last, Aronious summoned his dire wolf companion and, with no small amount of indignation from the gnome, carried Finkle-Hansel bodily from one store to the other, proving once and for all that they were the same person. Cornered, the gnome confessed. He had opened Strings and Sundries first, but business had been poor. Believing competition would drive customers, he opened a second shop — only to realize that selling different merchandise meant no competition at all. Now he had two failing businesses and no time to run either properly. The charade of being "cousins" was a desperate attempt to make the shops feel like a thriving family enterprise. Hobbins, ever practical, offered him advice: hire a clerk, merge the inventory, find something unique to sell. Anything but what he was doing now. The gnome's face lit with gratitude. He promised that the next time they visited, they wouldn't even recognize the place. The party set out into the wilderness, heading southeast toward the mountains where Skree made his lair. The wind bit at their faces, and the snow fell in thick, swirling curtains. Halfway to their destination, Aronious spotted tracks in the snow — fresh, large, unmistakable. Owlbear. He followed the prints to a small grove of pines, where the beast hunched over the carcass of a dead elk, tearing into it with savage hunger. Aronious crept closer, but a twig snapped beneath his boot. The owlbear's head jerked up, eyes scanning the treeline. With a flick of his wrist, Aronious hurled a stone into the opposite brush. The creature turned, distracted, and he slipped away unseen. They pressed onward. By the time they reached the cave, the storm had grown fierce. The entrance yawned before them, dark and uninviting, the air inside thick with the stench of rot and decay. They had barely stepped across the threshold when the chittering began. Three massive spiders emerged from the shadows, their legs clicking against stone, their eyes gleaming with hunger. Yin Shen's breath caught — her arachnophobia flared hot and sharp — but she steadied herself with a few deep breaths. Then her hands ignited with flame, and she hurled bolts of fire into the dark with reckless abandon. Hobbins' chromatic orb obliterated the carapace of the nearest spider in a burst of elemental fury. Aronious loosed arrows while his dire wolf tore into another, fangs flashing in the dim light. Yin Shen reached into her satchel and drew forth a small, furry ball. She hurled it at the farthest spider, and in a flash of magic, a giant badger materialized — snarling, clawing, biting with primal ferocity — before falling to the spider's venomous bite. When the last spider fell, silence returned. The party stood at the mouth of the cave, breath misting in the cold, the storm raging behind them and the dark unknown stretching ahead. Somewhere deeper within, Skree waited. And they would find him.

docs.text: Session 8: The Deranged Godling As a group, the party pressed deeper into the darkness beyond the spider den, their nerves still taut from the battle behind them. The air grew thick and stale, and from the shadows ahead came whispers — soft, maddening, threading through the black like silk. They discovered an alcove choked with refuse and the brittle husks of hatched spider eggs. Yin Shen spotted something metallic half-buried in the filth and pulled hard to free it. When it came loose, her face fell — a full breastplate, far too cumbersome for a rogue's trade. Aronious took it without hesitation. He scrubbed away the worst of the grime and strapped the plate over his leather armor, testing its weight with a satisfied nod. Wary of what lay ahead, Aronious sent his dire wolf companion forward to scout. The beast padded silently into the dark — until it stepped into a vast chamber alive with chaos. Hundreds of bats swarmed through the air in frantic spirals, their shrieks filling the stone. And at the center of it all, perched among the stalactites, was Skree . The godling was a horror to behold. His once-sleek fur was matted and torn, his body riddled with pustules and rot. Wounds wept across his wings and flanks, and a wrongness radiated from him — something deeper than madness, something corrupt . The moment Skree's eyes fixed on the wolf, he screeched with wild rage. The battle began. Yin Shen reached into her Gray Bag of Tricks and hurled a small furry ball into the fray. A giant rat materialized beside the wolf, chittering as it joined the fight. Aronious and his dire wolf moved as one — the ranger unleashing arrows and druidic magic from a distance while his companion tore at the swarming bats with fang and claw, ripping the winged beasts from the air. Hobbins conjured arcane power in her tiny paws, hurling thunderous orbs through the cavern. She had chosen her spells well — sound-based attacks that struck Skree with devastating force, exploiting his keen and fragile senses. Yin Shen darted between the shadows, striking with precision and thinning the endless flurry of bats that filled the chamber. Then Skree unleashed his rage. A sonic pulse exploded from the godling, shaking the cave walls and sending stone dust raining from above. The blast caught both Hobbins and Aronious. The ranger crumpled, thrown bodily to the ground and left motionless. Yin Shen dove behind a rock wall, narrowly escaping the worst of it. Seeing their companion fall ignited something fierce in both Hobbins and Yin Shen. With renewed fury, they doubled their assault — spell and blade flashing in tandem — until at last, Skree's tortured body fell from the air and crashed to the stone below. The godling lay still. The remaining bats scattered in all directions, fleeing into the dark recesses of the cave. Silence returned, broken only by the party's ragged breathing. With haste, Hobbins ran to Aronious and stabilized him there in the cave. Hobbins approached cautiously and retrieved Skree's Collar and charm from Skree's broken form — proof of their victory for Lupine. But even with the godling slain, the wrongness lingered. It clung to the air like a chill, prickling at the edges of their senses. This corruption had not come from Skree alone. Driven by instinct, the party explored deeper. In a shadowed alcove, they found it — a totem, twisted and dark, radiating the same foul energy that had poisoned the godling. Hobbins wrapped it carefully in cloth to dull its influence and stuffed it into her bag. With haste born of unease, the party turned and made for the exit. When they finally stepped out into the open air, the wind biting at their faces and the storm swirling around them, they breathed deeply — grateful to be free of the corrupted cavern and the madness that dwelled within. Behind them, the cave entrance yawned like a wound in the mountain. And somewhere to the north, Lupine waited.

docs.text: Session 9: The Chardalyn Thief The journey back to Easthaven was harrowing. The blizzard raged with relentless fury, wind tearing at their cloaks and snow blinding their path. Then, without warning, the mountain itself gave way. An avalanche thundered down the slope. Aronious didn't see it coming — caught off guard as the wall of white rushed toward them. Yin Shen spotted it just in time, bracing herself against the impact. But Hobbins , ever quick-thinking, thrust her paws forward and unleashed thunderwave directly into the avalanche's leading edge. The spell worked. The blast disrupted the snow's momentum, forcing it to flood around them rather than over them. Still, they were nearly buried. Yin Shen seized Hobbins and pulled her clear, then conjured flame for Aronious to use as a barrier against the crushing wind and snow. When the white settled, they stood — bruised, cold, but alive. By the time they reached Easthaven, dusk had fallen. Two glowing points of warmth marked the guard posts in the distance, welcoming beacons against the dark. The party made their way to Strings and Sundries to check on the gnome shopkeeper. Inside, they found him busily reorganizing inventory, a look of genuine contentment on his face. When pressed for his real name, he grew sheepish and admitted it: Polard Hinscrop . He was embarrassed by it — the name felt distinctly un-gnomish to his ears. Satisfied that their advice had taken root, the party left for the town hall. The streets were dark and eerily quiet. When they reached the town hall's entrance, they found the doors unlocked and slightly askew. Inside, the entryway was pitch black — no lanterns lit, no guards posted. Just the three of them, alone in the shadows. They moved cautiously through the clerk's offices and into the promenade — a grand chamber with stairs leading to the second floor. At its center stood a ship's figurehead, wooden and carved into the shape of a demon. In the creature's chest gaped an empty hole. The party investigated. Black crystalline shards littered the edges of the cavity, and splinters lay scattered on the floor below. Something had been embedded there — and violently torn free. Hobbins, growing anxious in the silence, returned to the main entrance and discovered the truth: the town hall was closed . The party was trespassing. But if the hall was closed, why were the doors unlocked and damaged? Regrouping, they agreed something was wrong. They descended to the lower dungeon level. Hobbins leapt onto the thick oaken door and wedged her dagger into the lock, prying and twisting with all her might until the mechanism broke and the door swung open. While the others finished investigating the mundane upper rooms — finding nothing of note — Hobbins pressed eastward down the dungeon corridor. At the end, she opened a door and froze. Inside were three guards, bound, gagged, and unconscious in the corner. The far wall had been caved in, and a crude tunnel led out to the frozen streets beyond. The party roused one of the guards and stabilized him. At first, he eyed them with suspicion, certain they were responsible. But Hobbins explained this was a "wrong place, right time" situation, and the guard's anger turned to alarm. Together, they returned upstairs. When the guard saw the damaged figurehead, he exclaimed that the Chardalyn crystal had been stolen — a large black crystal that had once jutted from the old ship's chest. Yin Shen crouched to examine the scene more closely. She spotted scattered crystal fragments leading into the corner of the room and followed the trail — until she collided with something unseen. In an instant, the invisibility shattered. Before her stood a Duergar — gray-skinned, bundled in furs and orange armor, with a clinking sack slung over his shoulder. He shoved Yin Shen backward and bolted for the exit. Hobbins reacted without hesitation, hurling magic missile at the fleeing thief. The bolts struck true, staggering him but not stopping his flight. Yin Shen sprinted after him but couldn't close the gap. Aronious lashed out with thorn whip , but the thorns cracked against empty air. Hobbins loosed another volley of magic missiles , each one striking with a grunt of pain from the Duergar. Yin Shen reached into her Gray Bag of Tricks and flung another furry ball. It bounced off the Duergar's shoulders, and a giant badger materialized, snarling and snapping at his heels. Aronious tried again with his whip — again, it struck only air. Hobbins, frustration mounting, conjured an acidic chromatic orb and hurled it with deadly precision. The sphere struck the Duergar's back, singeing his clothing and staggering him forward. Yin Shen threw herself bodily at the dwarf, wrapping her limbs around his and dragging him to the ground in a tangle of limbs and fury. Before he could recover, Hobbins sprinted over and — without pausing to think — rammed her dagger clean through his hand, pinning him to the floor. Together, they bound him with rope and hauled him before the guard. The interrogation began. The Duergar revealed that his people were stockpiling Chardalyn — though he would not say why. Yin Shen's mind flashed to the prophecy spoken by Hethyl Arkorran , the soothsayer of the Knights of the Black Sword : "A fortress, a villain, a crystal machine with a dragon's heart..." She leaned in and asked about a mechanical dragon. The Duergar's eyes darted side to side. Sweat beaded on his brow. He clenched his jaw and hissed through his teeth: "You'll get no more from me." And he spoke no further. The party left him with the guards to finish the interrogation and stepped back into the cold night air. Somewhere beneath the mountains, the Duergar were building something — something powered by Chardalyn, something vast and terrible. And the prophecy had warned them: if they did not stop it, the machine would burn away the Rime — and everything else with it.

docs.text: Black Lotus Sword Celestial blade — lost Yin Shen 's sword from her days as a goddess of trickery. A blade as dark as night, and silent like the grave. She fought with it in the shadows, coming in behind an enemy line while her twin Shuāng held its attention from the front. Paired with her kimono , nobody heard her coming — and by the time they did, it was already too late. Status Unrecovered. Tyr stripped it from her when he delivered judgement, along with her title, her magic, her immortality, and her kimono. He did not destroy any of it. He scattered her possessions across Icewind Dale . Finding them again is one of the two things Yin Shen has been working toward since the day she landed in the snow.

docs.text: Lantern of Tracking Wondrous item, common This hooded lantern burns for 6 hours on 1 pint of oil, shedding bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Each lantern of tracking is designed to track down a certain type of creature, which is determined by rolling on the Lantern of Tracking table. Once determined, this creature type can't be changed. While the lantern is within 300 feet of any creature of that type, its flame turns bright green. The lantern doesn't pinpoint the creature's exact location, however. docs.text: Auril's Island Island in the Sea of Moving Ice Auril 's own island, marked on a map by Dzaan at a point the Targos captain swore held no land at all. He set a course for it anyway. It is the current objective. The Codicil of White is kept here, and in it an incantation that can split the Reghed Glacier and open Ythryn . Approach The cold came on before the island did — biting, and wrong for the latitude. Then fog. The ship came out of it under cliffs of ice fifty feet high , with masts standing up out of the water around them and the ships they belonged to somewhere underneath. Ahead was a dock carved from ice, shattered, and built for giants . The crew anchored offshore and refused to land. They would wait one day; the second cost fifty gold, haggled down by first mate Dale to the ten already owed on return plus one magic item from whatever the party found ashore. Soppo's Tour An ice mephit named Soppo was waiting on the dock, waving and jabbering in Auran. Hobbins cast comprehend languages as a ritual and did the talking from there. Soppo offered to guide them. There is, by its account, plenty to see: Shipwrecks , full of goods A recent wreck with one survivor, who made it as far as the shore and froze there A field of ice sculptures Grimskalle , at the centre of the island, where the lady's book is kept, and where it is dangerous "Soppo hasn't had visitors in a while. Again, unless you count the one who crawled ashore, though she didn't last." Asked about Professor Skant , Soppo did not know the orb. Asked about the Codicil of White, it looked shocked. The tour runs fourteen hours, with Grimskalle at the end of it. The party accepted. Yin Shen kept her guard up.

docs.text: Blackiron Blades Smithy and outfitter This combination shop and smithy stands just north of the main square. Garn the Hammer manufactures the cheapest blades in Ten-Towns, while his sister Elza sells adventuring supplies—including rations, cold weather gear, ice picks, and snowshoes—to fortune-seekers. Most of the veteran sellswords in Ten-Towns disdain Garn's smithcraft, due to the uninspiring quality of his work. Jokes told about hapless newcomers to Icewind Dale often end with the line "an' 'e was carrying a Blackiron blade, to boot!"

docs.text: Dougan's Hole In a Nutshell Friendliness ❄ Services ❄ Comfort ❄ Population : 50 Leaders : Speaker Edgra Dermoot Militia : Sacrifice to Auril : Human The smallest and southernmost of Ten-Towns, on the shore of Redwaters. Torg's Trading Company travel vouchers explicitly do not service it. The Evacuation Dougan's Hole was first on the Chardalyn Dragon 's route — the channel cut through the stone map in Sunblight Fortress began here and ran north through Goodmead to Easthaven . The party worked out eight hours for the dragon, and eight hours for themselves in a straight line to Easthaven. That settled the question of rest. It did not settle the question of the two small towns in between. Goodmead had no speaker. Dougan's Hole had Edgra Dermoot , an old trapper woman. So it would be Edgra: Dougan's Hole would run for Easthaven and gather up Goodmead on the way. Hobbins cast sending from Aronious's arms as he ran for the dogsled. The answer came back curt. Dougan's Hole was leaving its houses where they stood. Around a hundred and fifty people from the two towns reached Easthaven's gate ahead of the dragon, carrying what they could. The dragon's flight bent away toward Dougan's Hole as the party's sled outran it north. Connections Overland Travel from Dougan's Hole To Travel Time Goodmead 5 hours Bryn Shander 11 hours

docs.text: Easthaven Town Hall Civic building, Easthaven Clerk's offices at the front, a grand promenade with stairs to the second floor, and a dungeon level below holding cells. The party has done more business here than anywhere else in Ten-Towns. At the centre of the promenade stands a ship's figurehead carved into the shape of a demon . A large black chardalyn crystal once jutted from its chest. The Theft The party found the doors unlocked and slightly askew one dark evening, the entryway pitch black, no lanterns lit and no guards posted. They were, as Hobbins worked out partway through, trespassing in a closed building — which raised the question of why the doors were unlocked and damaged. The figurehead's chest gaped empty, black crystalline shards around the cavity and splinters on the floor below. Three guards were found bound, gagged and unconscious in a lower room, with the far wall caved in and a crude tunnel leading out to the frozen streets. Yin Shen followed a trail of crystal fragments into a corner and collided with something unseen. The invisibility shattered, and a Duergar in furs and orange armour with a clinking sack over his shoulder shoved her back and bolted. They ran him down in the street and Hobbins pinned his hand to the floor with her dagger. The Cell He admitted his people were stockpiling chardalyn and would say no more. He did not stay. Yin Shen returned to the basement to find the dust disturbed, clear signs of struggle, and footprints leading toward the door, each one progressively smaller than the last , vanishing entirely at the threshold. That detail — recognised again in the snow behind an inn in Caer-Konig — is what unravelled the conspiracy. Authority This is where Captain Imdra Arlaggath read Torvus ' writ and added her own endorsement in wax, making the party agents of Easthaven in all but formal title. It is also where a later prisoner drove hidden chardalyn shards into his own flesh in confinement, and had to be put down. Yin Shen kicked the door in on her return from the north, shouting Imdra's name. Imdra was back on duty in a plain standard uniform.

docs.text: Easthaven In a Nutshell Friendliness ❄❄ Services ❄❄❄ Comfort ❄❄❄ Population : 750 Leaders : Speaker Danneth Waylen , Captain Imdra Arlaggath commands the town's militia. Militia : Roughly 150 soldiers 12 officers. Sacrifice to Auril : Human Heraldry A snowflake at the top center of a steel-gray field, above a horizontal brown field that forms the left-hand base, and a dark blue field that forms the right-hand base; where they meet is a thin white tower. The brown field represents the Eastway, the tower represents the town, and the blue field is Lac Dinneshere. Connections The Eastway stretches between Easthaven and Bryn Shander. Snow-covered paths branching off this road lead to Caer-Dineval and Goodmead. Travel times in the Overland Travel from Easthaven table assume that characters are on foot; mounts and dogsleds can shorten these times by as much as 50 percent. Overland Travel from Easthaven To Travel Time Bryn Shander 7½ hours Caer-Dineval 9 hours Goodmead 4½ hours Locations in Easthaven The Wet Trout The White Lady Inn Easthaven Town Hall — clerk's offices, a promenade with a demon-headed ship's figurehead at its centre, and a dungeon level below. The Chardalyn crystal was torn from the figurehead's chest by a Duergar thief who tunnelled out through the dungeon wall. The Coal Poker — the town smithy, across town near the White Lady Inn and the stables. The dwarves there do no enchanting themselves; they ship goods out for arcane modification and re-import them, and keep those connections secret because it is good for business. Hobbins traded lessons in rune-work to one of their apprentices for a steel helmet. The Musical Empolardium — Polard Hinscrop 's rebuilt instrument shop, formerly Strings and Sundries. See the Music Shop Conspiracy . The Easthaven Ferry — named in a captured Duergar letter as a base of operations for the search for chardalyn. The Dragon Attack Easthaven was struck twice. The first incursion was hard, fast, and purposeful: the great front gate was blackened by fire and split by a force that had not bothered to find a seam, and Captain Imdra Arlaggath was taken prisoner. The party saw the damage half-repaired in the cold as they rode past toward the Spine of the World. The second was the Chardalyn Dragon. Easthaven had eight hours' warning and spent it patching the walls with packed ice and snow and massing two hundred militia — a hundred and fifty in uniform and fifty who had simply turned up — alongside a hundred and fifty evacuees from Dougan's Hole and Goodmead. Radiant breath shattered a section of wall and took a part of the vanguard with it. By the time the dragon burst, the line had thinned to around eighty. The blast left a crater and a missing section of wall, and nothing in the crater but chardalyn fragments. On Aronious 's warning about what prolonged contact with the material does to a mind, Imdra put a task force on burying it and militia on keeping the townsfolk away. A whole district burned. Polard Hinscrop 's lane took the breath straight down it and not one building was left standing.

docs.text: Goodmead In a Nutshell Friendliness ❄❄❄ Services ❄ Comfort ❄❄ Population : 100 Leaders : vacant Militia : Sacrifice to Auril : Mead The Empty Seat Goodmead has no speaker. The last one died in a verbeeg incursion, and the seat has sat empty since while a handful of hopefuls reach for it — Drumly Hobbins , Hobbins 's father, among them. That vacancy mattered more than anyone expected. When the Chardalyn Dragon broke out of Sunblight Fortress and began following the route carved into Xardorok's stone map — Dougan's Hole , then Goodmead, then Easthaven — there was no one in Goodmead to send a warning to. The party sent it to Edgra Dermoot of Dougan's Hole instead, with instructions to gather Goodmead's people on the way past. Around a hundred and fifty people from the two towns made Easthaven's gate ahead of the dragon. Smoke stood in the sky from the direction of Goodmead as the party made their report on the wall. Locations in Goodmead The Magikal Morgue — the Hobbins family's magical curiosity shop, dealing in items recovered from the frozen wastes, and Hobbins 's childhood home. Run by Logely and Drumly Hobbins , and one of the reasons the family is among Goodmead's more prosperous households. Connections Snow-covered paths link Goodmead to Bryn Shander , Easthaven , Caer-Dineval , and Dougan's Hole . docs.text: Kelvin's Cairn Mountain The lone mountain of Icewind Dale , rising from the tundra north of the three lakes. Bitter winds blow down off it and across Lac Dinneshere , and dwarven mines work its stone. The Iron Shipment A shipment of iron bound for Blackiron Blades of Bryn Shander was lost on the mountain when the dwarves carrying it down from the mines were attacked by a yeti . Aronious heard about it over the bar at The Wet Trout . The smiths offered gold for its return, and friendship besides — which for a dwarf is often worth more. The load has never been recovered. The Duergar Stronghold Following footprints and dogsled tracks northeast out of Caer-Konig , the party found a stronghold carved directly into the stone at the mountain's base — the first hard evidence that the Duergar conspiracy was real. Inside they found a guard outpost with no external entrance, a trapdoor and tunnel running under the wall, a larger-than-normal dogsled, a zombie ogre caged beside the goats stolen from Caer-Konig, a spiked corridor trap, holding cells where denizens of Ten-Towns had been transformed into fungal monsters , and the magic lantern taken from The Northern Light . A Duergar in finery rather than armor was pinned in the spike trap and interrogated. In Dwarvish, he bellowed: My father is more powerful than any of you filthy creatures could imagine! You don't understand the glory of it, the power found in the ice. None of you do. But you will learn soon enough when my father unleashes his terror upon Ten-Towns! Your doom soars on dragon's wings! A crumpled letter found in his room pointed to the next base: Brother, You will find me on the frozen ferry in Easthaven. From this new base, the search for chardalyn continues. Long may our father reign over this dark land! — Durth The father was Xardorok Sunblight. The dragon was real. The Ravine On the approach, in a ravine short of the mountain, the party found the back half of a polar bear taken in a single bite — and then a snowdrift that shifted and fell away to reveal the head and neck of an ancient white dragon , a saddle peeking from the snow with a robed figure strapped into it, unmoving. They crept past without waking it. On the return trip it had been re-buried by fresh drifts.

Inside they found a guard outpost with no external entrance, a trapdoor and tunnel running under the wall, a larger-than-normal dogsled, a zombie ogre caged beside the goats stolen from Caer-Konig, a spiked corridor trap, holding cells where denizens of Ten-Towns had been transformed into fungal monsters , and the magic lantern taken from The Northern Light . A Duergar in finery rather than armor was pinned in the spike trap and interrogated. In Dwarvish, he bellowed: My father is more powerful than any of you filthy creatures could imagine! You don't understand the glory of it, the power found in the ice. None of you do. But you will learn soon enough when my father unleashes his terror upon Ten-Towns! Your doom soars on dragon's wings! A crumpled letter found in his room pointed to the next base: Brother, You will find me on the frozen ferry in Easthaven. From this new base, the search for chardalyn continues. Long may our father reign over this dark land! — Durth The father was Xardorok Sunblight. The dragon was real.
docs.title: The Duergar Stronghold

docs.text: On the approach, in a ravine short of the mountain, the party found the back half of a polar bear taken in a single bite — and then a snowdrift that shifted and fell away to reveal the head and neck of an ancient white dragon , a saddle peeking from the snow with a robed figure strapped into it, unmoving. They crept past without waking it. On the return trip it had been re-buried by fresh drifts.
docs.title: The Ravine

docs.text: Musical Empolardium Instrument shop, Easthaven Polard Hinscrop 's rebuilt music shop, successor to Strings and Sundries and Drums Emporium both — see the Music Shop Conspiracy for how it got that way. The old shop and the whole of its lane were destroyed when the Chardalyn Dragon 's radiant breath went straight down it. Polard knelt in the rubble and wept, then produced the insurance pamphlet the party had given him and showed them the last unchecked box. "I never got it notarized." A week later the plot was twice its old size, Easthaven's thanks for his part in the defense — a tent, a sign, a freshly built workbench, and no merchandise of any kind. The Shop Now Bigger than the old one and about half finished. Polard has hired an assistant named Samantha to work the counter, and means to install a forge and train with the Easthaven blacksmith so he can supply the party's gear himself. The party offered a better name for the place. It was a pun. Polard did not need to think about it. "Samantha, we need to change the sign immediately." The Sign Hobbins went up on the roof to help with the sign, and tried to unhook it to prove she was helping. The sign won. It took her off the roof with it and into a snowbank. Polard charged her one gold for the breakage, and winked at Aronious .

docs.text: Sea of Moving Ice Frozen sea north of Icewind Dale A frozen expanse broken by pressure ridges and deep blue fissures, stretching away under a sky that seems to press down rather than lift. It announces itself gradually and then all at once: the ground grows harder, the air sharper, and the horizon shows the grey-white suggestion of pack ice. The Shipwreck One of the ancient white dragon 's lairs. The hull rises from the ice at a list, half-consumed by the freeze, every timber grey and salt-stripped, and opened by something that had simply decided a wall was an inconvenience. Inside: a frost troll, four kobolds in a barricaded room, and the dragon's hoard glimmering under the ice. Tinjong 's cave is within running distance of it, and the party reached it ahead of a rain of falling ice spears. Sailing North There is no port on this sea that Ten-Towns can offer. Easthaven has no real sailors and no water that leads here; Captain Imdra Arlaggath sent the party to the taverns of Targos for a captain instead. The nearest port Dzaan knew of is Revel's End , which is a prison, and the white dragon lies in the way regardless. The crossing from Targos runs a day of breaking ice upriver and two days at sea. Legend offers an alternative: Angajuk's Bell , a bronze bell on the shore that is said to summon a giant whale with a wrecked ship on its back, awakened once by a frost druid to carry travelers. Hazards The cold comes on wrong before the ice does — biting, and too hard for the latitude, as the Targos captain observed. Then fog, and a great deal of it. Under cliffs of ice fifty feet high, masts stand up out of the water with the ships they belong to somewhere underneath. The crew that carried the party refused to land and would wait only one day without renegotiating. "What do you think sunk these ships? I don't see them stuck on any rocks." Destinations Auril's Island , marked on Dzaan's map at a spot the captain swore held no land at all

docs.text: Spine of the World Mountain range The great range along the southern edge of Icewind Dale , separating the Dale from the lands below. Its passes are the only land route in or out, and they are not safe ones — Spellix Romwood 's caravan was ambushed by goblins in the pass to the west, and The Goblin Stronghold sits in a ravine carved into the rock nearby. The Stronghold in the Spine Deep in these mountains, Xardorok Sunblight built Sunblight Fortress and the forge that made the Chardalyn Dragon . Its location came out of a Duergar captured during the failed incursion on Termalaine , and reached the party through Speaker Oarus Masthew in the same breath as the news that Easthaven had been hit and Captain Imdra Arlaggath taken. Aronious guided the party up with a ranger's instinct, reading the terrain and steering them clear of the worst of it — the hidden drops, the unstable slopes, the places where the snow moved. They climbed until the foothills gave way to raw stone and the fortress rose above them without warning.
docs.title: Spine of the World

docs.text: Sunblight Fortress Duergar stronghold, Spine of the World Xardorok Sunblight 's seat, and the forge where the Chardalyn Dragon was built. Sheer walls carved directly from the mountain's body, arrowslits running its face in rows and glowing faintly from within, and a narrow ice-slicked stair up the side to a single large stone door. Its location came from a Duergar captured during the failed incursion on Termalaine . The Entrance The door had not been opened for the party. It had been set . A lock disengaged from somewhere within as they approached, and the crossbow bolt came through the arrowslit the moment they stepped inside. Nine Duergar in the flanking barracks were already on their feet and already enlarging, filling the narrow hall with grey iron bulk. The space gave nothing away — too tight for Mylbor and Polard to bring their considerable capacity to bear. Hobbins made it work anyway, ricocheting chromatic orbs from one grey body to the next, while Aronious plugged the corridor with the Shield Guardian and Yin Shen scattered caltrops across the threshold. Upper Level The map room. A relief map carved from solid stone — Ten-Towns in precise miniature, the surrounding wilderness etched down to individual ridgelines, and a channel cut between all ten settlements in a continuous loop. A dragon figurine sits on an iron pole in the channel, and a crank on the side walks it around the circuit. Someone had been plotting the route for a long time. Private quarters. A large ornate bed and a chest of gem-encrusted garments. A hatch in the chest's bottom triggered as the last item cleared it and flooded the room with poison gas . Hobbins held the door shut from the inside and would not let go until Yin Shen's voice, then Aronious's, then Polard's, in sequence, finally reached her. Yin Shen came through gasping and lay on the stone for some time. A hidden closet off the map room, holding several mind flayer skulls arranged around a chardalyn statuette. Hobbins shot the statuette apart. Yin Shen touched one of the skulls and stood perfectly still — to the party nothing happened; to her, time ran forward through days, weeks, and then ages, an accelerating pull dragging her northward while something vast and cold unwound around her. She came back the way a candle relights, all at once, and said nothing. Grandolpha Muzgardt 's dining room , in the western hallway. Lower Level Reached by a service elevator, past throne room guards bearing Xardorok's sigil who refused an unscheduled shift rotation without a word and without moving. The main forge is a cavern swimming in heat and smoke, forty feet at the ceiling's peak and pressed down to twenty along the southern wall. At its centre stands a pyramid forge ten feet tall with its apex sheared off, radiating ripples of firelight and emitting a slow deep pulse from within its stone, like something breathing. A trough runs east from its base with black anvils ranged along either side. The dragon was chained beneath an opening in the ceiling, ringed by chanting Duergar. The cells held Captain Imdra Arlaggath . Afterward Xardorok fell beside the lever he was still pulling. The dragon broke its chains and flew north. Steel was still meeting steel beyond the walls as the party took the elevator up to the machinery room at the top, open to the sky — the sound of a fortress deciding who it belonged to. Nobody stayed to learn how it came out. Imdra's own gear never came back out of the building.

docs.text: Targos In a Nutshell Friendliness ❄❄ Services ❄❄❄ Comfort ❄❄ Population : 1000 Leaders : Speaker Naerth Maxildanarr Militia : Sacrifice to Auril : Human Connections Targos sits on Maer Dualdon , two hours' walk from Bryn Shander and the same from Bremen , though heavy snow has obliterated the Bremen trail. Mounts and dogsleds can shorten these times by as much as 50 percent. Overland Travel from Targos To Travel Time Bryn Shander 2 hours Bremen 2 hours Termalaine 4 hours The Port Targos is where Ten-Towns keeps its sailors. Captain Imdra Arlaggath sent the party here when they needed passage to the Sea of Moving Ice: Easthaven had no real sailors and no water that led north, and what they wanted was the taverns of Targos and a captain willing to take the work. The caravan run from Easthaven through Bryn Shander to Targos takes a little over nine hours. Targos fishing crews work the ice floes of Maer Dualdon and are not uniformly welcoming. One Targos vessel jeered the party off the water during the hunt for the awakened plesiosaur, and settled only when Hobbins threw a gold coin into the boat and let the crew fight over it. Locations in Targos Three Flags Sailing — the tavern where the party found their captain. A one-eyed man with a pipe laughed them out of the room when they asked for passage onto the Sea of Moving Ice, and told them they might as well ring Angajuk's Bell — a bronze bell on the shore, the story goes, and a giant whale with a wrecked ship on its back, awakened once by a frost druid to carry travelers. Ring the one and the other comes. The laughing stopped when Yin Shen said the voyage was meant to end the frost and that they were the ones who had killed the dragon. It was the first mate, Dale , who talked the captain into it. The crew muddled the price on purpose; Dale shook on thirty-five gold, with ten more due on return.

docs.text: Termalaine Mines Gem workings, Termalaine The tourmaline mines that put a gemstone on Termalaine's heraldry. Kobolds moved in, miners went missing, and the guild refused all work until the mine was cleared — a fifty gold notice on the Gelp board that sat unclaimed long enough for the party to walk past it twice. A sign at the entrance read, in handwriting far too precise and deliberate to belong to any miner: NO ENTRY — KOBOLDS ONLY Inside The upper tunnels reward careful attention; a few gemstones come loose from the walls with patient work. One Yin Shen pried out was valued near a hundred gold by the mine's own appraiser, who made no secret of wanting to buy it. The workings centre on a shaft that drops away into nothing , a waterfall somewhere below filling the silence with white noise, traced by a narrow wooden walkway that is more suggestion than structure. Hobbins pressed herself to the planks, heard sawing beneath the roar, looked over the edge at two kobolds working their blades through the timber supports, and cast thunderwave straight down. Deeper in, a chamber of gemstones clustered in cold colour — and a grell , which descended from the ceiling without sound and was dispatched by a group that had stopped being surprised by things dropping from above. Its tentacles became Yin Shen 's whip, cured by Karthax . The Possession A crack in the stone at the far end opened onto a cramped space where the remaining kobolds had made themselves at home. One did the talking — clearly, fluently, with a precision that sat entirely wrong in a kobold's mouth, and wearing wings that were not real. It was possessed . Something was riding behind its eyes and speaking through its throat. Hobbins' hand darted out, came away with a dirty pouch from its belt, and she walked to the edge of the central shaft and dropped it in. The ghost erupted from the kobold like steam from a wound, shrieking, and plunged after it into the dark. Also found here: a mind flayer's skull holding the psi crystal that would later get a nautiloid off the ground. The Mine Now The kobolds, freed of whatever had been steering them into banditry, wanted very little — warmth, food, and somewhere to be that wasn't a frozen mine shaft. Yin Shen offered them work in the mines for Termalaine free of charge, in exchange for meals and lodging in town. Foreman Lancastor thought about it. Speaker Oarus Masthew accepted it. The mine works a kobold crew now.

docs.text: The Mines — gem workings running deep under the town, around a central shaft with no apparent bottom and a waterfall somewhere below it. Kobolds moved in and miners went missing; a sign at the entrance read NO ENTRY — KOBOLDS ONLY in handwriting far too precise to belong to any miner. The party cleared it, freed the kobolds from the ghost steering them, and the mine now works a kobold crew paid in food and lodging. The mining offices — Foreman Lancastor 's desk, and the mine's own appraiser, a wiry balding man with a nasal voice who valued a single tunnel-wall gemstone at close to a hundred gold. The armorer — a dragonborn named Karthax , who cured a set of grell tentacles and lashed them into a serviceable whip overnight.
docs.title: Locations in Termalaine

docs.text: The Black Spire Netherese ruin — also called Dzaan's tower A structure jutting roughly twenty feet out of the frozen earth in the wilderness northeast of Caer-Konig , its walls perfectly smooth and deeply black. Not dark — black , in the way that swallows the grey light of an overcast sky rather than reflecting it. No snow clings to its surface. The party reached it from a map Randy Grailden sold Yin Shen for twenty gold, navigating by having the sled dogs track the scent of Dzaan 's fireball scroll across an ocean of featureless white. Scouts dispatched by Captain Imdra Arlaggath had confirmed only that something was out there, and that it was not natural. Upside Down Something turned the spire over. The first room inside is inverted : everything that once rested on the floor now dangles from what the party stood on, or lies broken where it fell, while anything bolted down remains fixed to what is now the ceiling. Yin Shen gathered texts on the Netherese empire from the fallen shelves, written in hands long dead. The Laboratory A hole in the floor leads down to a wizard's laboratory — shattered glass across every surface, strange liquids pooled and mingled in colours that don't have names, equipment broken and scattered, experiments interrupted by whatever catastrophe inverted the place. A chest bolted to what had been the floor hangs from the ceiling here. Yin Shen picked its lock at an uncomfortable angle and caught all four falling phials before one could shatter: four potions of resistance . A ruined bedchamber nearby holds the corpse of a long-dead wizard and an invisible, locked chest that keeps its contents in temporal stasis — airtight, watertight, fixed at a constant temperature. The leather-bound book inside crumbled to ash the instant it left, experiencing two thousand years in moments. Hobbins kept the chest and has since ridden out a radiant catastrophe inside it. The Occupants The spire was not empty. Black slimes with acid-soaked pseudopods nearly killed Hobbins on the level below. Deeper still was Dzaan 's simulacrum , working over parchment with an undead attendant named Krintas , muttering about failed experiments and a missing lifespark . "Dammit — all experiments failed. I need a lifespark." He warned them, before they went down: "Just a warning before going further, there are a few experiments below. Do avoid using acid, cold, or lightning while down there!" The Netherese Machine At the lowest level is a chamber of runes etched across the walls and apparatus, cracked deeply through the stone and flickering with instability. A central platform and a pedestal. Its first use made the simulacrum fully corporeal . The vortex destabilised, radiant energy erupted in a violent flash, Yin Shen and Aronious were struck by bolts, and Krintas took the worst of it — hurled into a wall, flesh scorched and smouldering. Its second use turned a detailed minor illusion of a blowgun with poisoned and sleep-laced darts into a real blowgun and real darts , clattering onto the stone floor without any radiant backlash at all. "One use left, maybe," Hobbins warned. The party chose to save it. The machine has one use remaining, the damage is worsening, and nobody has yet decided what it is for.
docs.title: The Black Spire

docs.text: The Caer Castle residence of the town speaker A sturdy, stone castle devoid of warmth and ostentation squats atop the cliffs overlooking the town and the frozen harbor. Warding the castle entrance are thick, battle-hardened wooden doors. Four cylindrical guard towers have wind-worn flags bearing the town's heraldry fluttering above their tiled, conical roofs. These towers are connected by icy battlements and parapets. Atop the castle walls and within the guard towers, torches flicker.

docs.text: The Goblin Stronghold Ruin, Spine of the World A goblin settlement built into an interior clearing at the end of a ravine carved into the mountain rock — watchtowers, timber walls, and the whole crude architecture of a community dug in and making itself permanent. The guards paid far more attention to the braziers beside them than to the perimeter. The Shield Guardian hung at its centre from rope and timber like a puppet with its strings cut. That is what brought the party, following the pull of Dzaan 's amulet. The Chief Yin Shen walked up to the gates as though she had every right to be there, took an arrow in the ground at her feet, and announced they were expected. The gates opened to reveal a larger goblin astride a worg. "Are you the emissaries?" She agreed that they were. The chief turned out to be Spellix Romwood , a gnome merchant in a goblin mask who had been trying to free his captured caravan and had stumbled into the role of chief instead. He was certain several of the elders had seen through him. Polard Hinscrop had to be disguised as a dwarf on the way in — goblins and gnomes being natural enemies, and a dwarf being better odds. The Fire The plan was to wait for dusk and move on the Guardian in the dark. It went poorly from the moment the construct activated. Every door, shutter, and dark gap in the timber walls disgorged goblins at once — not a patrol, not a garrison, a horde, with arrows coming not in volleys but in a constant hissing sheet. The worgs hit hardest, coordinated in a way that felt almost deliberate. It was not a battle the party could win. Yin Shen made the call, secured a rope and grappling hook at the battlements, and held the exit with a blade until everyone was down it. Before that, Hobbins looked back at the stronghold. Then she set it on fire. As the last of the party hit the ground outside, the shouts within split — half still howling pursuit, half now screaming at the fire spreading hungrily through the timber buildings. Behind them, somewhere in the mountain, the stronghold burned.

docs.text: The Magikal Morgue Magical curiosity shop, Goodmead The Hobbins family's shop, and Hobbins 's childhood home. Despite the name, the business is perfectly legitimate — if a little unsettling to first-time visitors. The family buys magical items recovered from the frozen wastes, whether salvaged from the remains of unlucky adventurers or sold on by the rare survivors who make it back alive. Every item is carefully catalogued, restored where restoration is possible, and sold to collectors, travellers, and aspiring adventurers. It has made the Hobbins family one of the more prosperous households in Goodmead. The Proprietors Logely Hobbins — mother. Handles the books and the negotiations with sharp precision. Drumly Hobbins — father. An uncanny eye for an authentic magical relic, and one of the hopefuls reaching for Goodmead's empty speaker's seat. Both love their daughter and consider her career an unnecessary gamble. In their view, adventurers are future customers — or else future inventory. They spent years watching ambitious heroes throw away promising futures chasing treasure and return broke, or not return at all. Magic is valuable and knowledge is valuable, but risking your life for either is foolish when you could study and trade them instead. They sent Hobbins to the magical academies of Waterdeep expecting a scholar, an enchanter, or a merchant capable of expanding the business far beyond Icewind Dale. Every letter since has politely encouraged her to come to her senses and return to it. What Hobbins Intends She grew up surrounded by enchanted trinkets, cursed curiosities, and stories of impossible adventures, and she loved all of it. One day she means to walk back through the door carrying artifacts no merchant could ever have purchased, because nobody else had ever found them.

docs.text: The Northern Light Inn The inn gets its name from a magic lantern that once hung above the front door. The inn is kept by the Shorard sisters . The Lantern The inn is named for a magic colour-changing lantern that once hung above the front door. It was stolen — the most visible of a string of thefts that Torvus spent a long time failing to solve, and that Cori would not let him hear the end of. The thieves were Duergar . Allie found the same shrinking footprints in the snow behind the storeroom that the party had seen in an Easthaven jail cell. The party recovered the lantern from the Duergar stronghold at Kelvin's Cairn and returned it, along with a bound prisoner and the beginnings of a much larger story.

The Climb serves hot chowder but is all out of beer and spirits, which might explain why locals don't frequent the place as much as they used to. The proprietor is a rugged middle-aged man named Roark.

docs.text: The Violet Hold Inn Unverified — an open lead A name on a violet slip of paper, pressed into the party's hands by a dark-robed stranger who slipped out of the crowd on a frozen Easthaven street. "The Violet Hold Inn may have what you seek. They specialize in moving objects of power." He tried to vanish immediately. Yin Shen and Hobbins stopped him and pulled his hood down, and found only a hunched elderly courier who knew just enough to be suspicious and not enough to be useful. The party let him go with more questions than answers. The lead came while they were trying to work out what the temporal stasis chest from The Black Spire could do, having just been offered scrap value for it by a dwarven smith who thought it would make a breastplate or two. Unresolved The party has never gone to the Violet Hold Inn. Its location is unknown, nobody has confirmed it exists, and nobody has explained how a stranger knew what they were carrying.

docs.text: Three Flags Sailing Tavern, Targos The tavern where ships are chartered out of Targos, and where the party found the only crew willing to sail onto the Sea of Moving Ice . Yin Shen looked the room over and settled on a large man with one eye and a pipe. A captain. She asked him for passage. The whole table laughed. She might as well ring Angajuk 's Bell, he told her — a bronze bell on the shore, and a giant whale with a wrecked ship on its back, awakened once by a frost druid to carry travelers. Ring the one and the other comes. Then Yin Shen said the voyage was meant to end the frost, and that they were the ones who had killed the dragon. The laughing stopped. The captain turned to his crew, and it was his first mate Dale who talked him into it. The crew muddled the price on purpose. Dale shook on thirty-five gold , paid before sailing — with ten more, the quartermaster mentioned at the dock, due on return.
docs.title: Three Flags Sailing

docs.text: Ythryn Buried Netherese city A city of the Netherese Empire lying buried in the Reghed Glacier . It is what Dzaan has been doing in Icewind Dale all along — the thing he never mentioned while traveling with the party as "Gustavo." He told them only after the ceremorphs' ship left the valley, standing in the snow as a blue translucent projection with the landscape visible through him. The Seal Auril 's magic guards the ice over the city. Fire will not open it, and neither will a pick. A book will. On Auril's Island , out in the Sea of Moving Ice , there is a tome called the Codicil of White , and in it an incantation that can split the glacier. The Contract Dzaan wants two things: The Codicil of White, retrieved from the island Professor Skant , his professor orb and an expert on the Netherese Empire, stolen from him The payoff is the city itself, and whatever magic is still lying around in it. The party took the job. He marked the island on their map.

docs.text: Angajuk Awakened whale — legend A giant whale with a wrecked ship on its back, awakened once by a frost druid to carry travelers across the Sea of Moving Ice . There is a bronze bell on the shore , the story goes. Ring the one and the other comes. The party heard it at Three Flags Sailing in Targos , from a one-eyed captain who had just finished laughing at the idea of sailing onto the Sea of Moving Ice. Asking for passage, he told Yin Shen , she might as well ring Angajuk's Bell. He meant it as a dismissal. Aronious liked the sound of it. The party chartered a ship instead, and the bell has not been rung. Note A frost druid awakening creatures across Icewind Dale is a familiar pattern — see Ravison and Godlings and Divine Energy . Whether Angajuk is her work or an older story has not been established.

docs.text: Aronious III Once a paladin serving faithfully to the pantheon above. He discarded his vows and took to the frozen wilderness to find and aid Yin Shen — and in the years since, the oath has found its way back to him by a different road. Before the Dale Aronious was raised in a city bound to its pantheon by a bargain: blessings and miracles in exchange for offerings, faith, and protection. He grew up watching divine intervention happen in front of him, over and over, and the amazement of it hardened into something steadier — a determination to protect the thing that had inspired him. He joined the Order charged with exactly that duty, and in time became strong and respected enough to be given a shrine of his own to guard. The shrines were where the bargain was kept. Without them that half of the arrangement failed, and the gods' mercy could turn sour. It was among the greatest honors the Order could confer. His posting was not what he expected. It sat in the outskirts, far from the dense part of the city, and it was small. The offerings heaped at it were children's toys and scrap — whoopie cushions, horns, a little rune that delivered a shock during a handshake. Something peeked out from behind the shrine as he took up his post: a small creature, something like a fox, sneering at him before vanishing into the air. It was Yin Shen 's shrine. The post had stood empty because its goddess had pranked every paladin before him into abandoning it. Aronious stayed. Across the following years the two of them grew close, and he made it his business to keep her mischief inside bounds a city could live with. "Because We Have Declared As Such" Then she was gone. One day he was cleaning up after a pie-trap that had made a small mess; the next there was no trace of her at all. He prayed to the pantheon for an explanation. For anything. What came back was a single sentence in the language of the divine, spoken directly into his mind: "because we have declared as such, that is all" He went to the floor. These were the gods he had given his life to protect — the beings who had inspired him as a child — and they would exile one of their own without so much as a reason, and tell him it was not his to ask. The goddess he had spent years guarding and befriending, no less. He left the Order, the city, and the duty that had just become meaningless, with two things clear in his mind: find Yin Shen, and find his own purpose. The road gave him the rest. He learned the bow. He learned what the druids know about the natural world. He learned to survive in places that do not care whether he does. After crossing several nations, the trail turned toward a land of cold and blizzards, where winter had swallowed grass that once ran green to the horizon. Ten-Towns. The tip that sent him there came from a civilian who had been zapped by a small lightning rune hidden in a handshake — unmistakably her work. He reached Bryn Shander cold and out of breath, pushed through the door of The Northlook Inn , and found her at last, in the company of a ferret who was drinking out of a tankard roughly her own size. docs.text: Once a paladin serving faithfully to the pantheon above. He discarded his vows and took to the frozen wilderness to find and aid Yin Shen — and in the years since, the oath has found its way back to him by a different road.
docs.title: Aronious III

docs.text: Aronious was raised in a city bound to its pantheon by a bargain: blessings and miracles in exchange for offerings, faith, and protection. He grew up watching divine intervention happen in front of him, over and over, and the amazement of it hardened into something steadier — a determination to protect the thing that had inspired him. He joined the Order charged with exactly that duty, and in time became strong and respected enough to be given a shrine of his own to guard. The shrines were where the bargain was kept. Without them that half of the arrangement failed, and the gods' mercy could turn sour. It was among the greatest honors the Order could confer. His posting was not what he expected. It sat in the outskirts, far from the dense part of the city, and it was small. The offerings heaped at it were children's toys and scrap — whoopie cushions, horns, a little rune that delivered a shock during a handshake. Something peeked out from behind the shrine as he took up his post: a small creature, something like a fox, sneering at him before vanishing into the air. It was Yin Shen 's shrine. The post had stood empty because its goddess had pranked every paladin before him into abandoning it. Aronious stayed. Across the following years the two of them grew close, and he made it his business to keep her mischief inside bounds a city could live with.
docs.title: Before the Dale

docs.text: Then she was gone. One day he was cleaning up after a pie-trap that had made a small mess; the next there was no trace of her at all. He prayed to the pantheon for an explanation. For anything. What came back was a single sentence in the language of the divine, spoken directly into his mind: "because we have declared as such, that is all" He went to the floor. These were the gods he had given his life to protect — the beings who had inspired him as a child — and they would exile one of their own without so much as a reason, and tell him it was not his to ask. The goddess he had spent years guarding and befriending, no less. He left the Order, the city, and the duty that had just become meaningless, with two things clear in his mind: find Yin Shen, and find his own purpose. The road gave him the rest. He learned the bow. He learned what the druids know about the natural world. He learned to survive in places that do not care whether he does. After crossing several nations, the trail turned toward a land of cold and blizzards, where winter had swallowed grass that once ran green to the horizon. Ten-Towns. The tip that sent him there came from a civilian who had been zapped by a small lightning rune hidden in a handshake — unmistakably her work. He reached Bryn Shander cold and out of breath, pushed through the door of The Northlook Inn , and found her at last, in the company of a ferret who was drinking out of a tankard roughly her own size. He hugged her. Then he hit her on the head and demanded to know what she thought she was doing. Source Condensed from the player's own text — see Aronious III — Player Backstory .
docs.title: "Because We Have Declared As Such"

docs.text: Captain Imdra Arlaggath Captain of the Easthaven Militia A stern, clear-eyed commander who moves faster than the people around her and knows it. She has been the party's most consistent institutional ally in Ten-Towns, and the one who paid for that alliance most dearly. Party Interactions She first met Yin Shen in the square as Dzaan burned, and on learning that Sephek Kaltro was dead she set them on the missing fishermen of Lac Dinneshere , paying out Dzaan's confiscated effects as the reward. When the party first brought her the prophecy of a crystal machine with a dragon's heart, she could not believe it, and would not carry wild claims to the Speaker without proof. The writ from Torvus of Caer-Konig changed that. She read it, wrote that the party was working under official business of Captain Imdra and Easthaven , and pressed her signet into the wax. She promised notices to every town speaker and warned that it would take time — not everyone moved as quickly as she did. She was right about the threat and wrong about having it contained. The captured Duergar had hidden chardalyn shards on his person and drove them into his own flesh in confinement; the guards put down what was left of him. She accepted responsibility for the failed interrogation and asked the party's forgiveness. By then three more towns were reinforcing their militias, and half of Ten-Towns stood in some state of readiness. Capture and Return Easthaven was hit hard, fast, and with purpose, and Imdra was taken. The party learned of it from Oarus Masthew in Termalaine , along with the location of the stronghold in the Spine of the World that a captured Duergar had given up. They found her in the cells beneath Xardorok Sunblight's fortress, opened the lock, and put a weapon in her hand before anyone said much else. She looked at them with the expression of someone filing away questions for later, and nodded that she was ready. She rode back with them for the eight-hour run to Easthaven and left to join the commanders at the wall, bent over the maps while the Chardalyn Dragon came in. Afterward Aronious warned her what prolonged contact with chardalyn does to a mind — a kind of necrosis — and that the fragments in the crater should be buried rather than handled. She put a task force on the cleanup and militia on the site. She is back on duty in a plain standard uniform. Her own gear never came back out of the fortress.

docs.text: Cori and Allie Human sisters Owners of The Northern Light Inn. Kind and caring of their town speaker. The younger, Allie, is lithe and charming; she greets guests and does all the cleaning. The older, Cori, is stout and scowling; she sees to the inn's provisioning and handles all the cooking. The Lantern The magic lantern that gave the inn its name was stolen, and Torvus ' failure to recover it had become a standing joke at his expense. It was Allie who connected the party's account of shrinking footprints in an Easthaven jail cell to the same prints in the snow behind her own storeroom, and who went white when she heard it. She wrote out her account and gave her name as testimony. Cori, meanwhile, was pouring Hobbins a glass of something clear off the top shelf before Aronious could stop her, and then handed him a rag and pointed at the floor without a word. They offered free room and board while the party investigated. They had no coin for a reward, and said so plainly. When the lantern came back, they rummaged through their belongings and produced a purse holding three gold and six silver — all of it. "We're sorry we don't have more to offer you. Times is rough with the winter's Rime shuttering travel, trade, and the joy in our hearts. This is all we have left." — Cori "We can offer you rooms and food free of charge whenever you visit!" — Allie That offer still stands.

His office was empty when the party reached it. Only tax documents and scattered parchment were on the desk.

docs.text: Dale First mate, out of Targos First mate aboard the ship the party chartered at Three Flags Sailing for the crossing to Auril's Island , and the only reason that charter happened at all. The captain — a large one-eyed man with a pipe — laughed Yin Shen out of the room when she asked for passage onto the Sea of Moving Ice , and told her she might as well ring Angajuk 's Bell. The laughing stopped when she said the voyage was meant to end the frost and that they were the ones who had killed the dragon. The captain turned to his crew. It was Dale who talked him into it. Terms Dale has done all the party's negotiating since, generally against the interests of his own crew. The crew muddled the price on purpose. Dale shook Yin Shen's hand on thirty-five gold , paid before sailing. The quartermaster later informed her that ten more would be due on return — more than she thought she had shaken on. At the island the crew refused to land and would wait one day. The party wanted two, and the quartermaster shoved the captain aside to name the price of the second: fifty gold. The haggling went on for some time, and Aronious appealed to legend. It was Dale, again, who gave. Two days, the ten gold on return as agreed, and one magic item out of whatever the party finds on the island.

docs.text: Dredavex Ceremorph, gnome-sized The ceremorph at the helm of the crashed nautiloid, working at a control panel beneath a lattice of glowing jellyfish. Yin Shen 's owl familiar found somewhere to hide on the upper deck and watched for some time without being noticed. When the trade for the psi crystal was agreed, it was Dredavex who brought out a small chitinous chest. Inside were a pair of crystal lenses and a helmet shaped like an owl, capped with something very like a brain. Hobbins tried the lenses first. They were too big for her and far from comfortable, but she could see in the dark and pick out more of what she was looking at. The helmet wanted attunement, so she took both off again. They proved to be Eyes of Minute Seeing and a Helm of Telepathy . Dredavex left with Voren and the ship, bound for the Astral realm.
