docs.text: Durth Duergar, son of Xardorok Sunblight Known to the party only through a crumpled letter found in the Duergar stronghold at Kelvin's Cairn , written to the brother who was holding that outpost: Brother, You will find me on the frozen ferry in Easthaven. From this new base, the search for chardalyn continues. Long may our father reign over this dark land! — Durth That letter is what connected the thefts in Caer-Konig and Easthaven to a single operation, and gave Captain Imdra Arlaggath something concrete enough to act on. The Easthaven ferry was named as a base of operations. His brother at the Kelvin's Cairn outpost — the Duergar in finery, pinned in the spike trap — was the one who bellowed the boast about their father's dragon. Durth's own fate is unrecorded. He was not among the dead at Sunblight Fortress so far as the party knows.

docs.text: Dzaan Human Wizard A red-robed wizard of Thay, burned at the stake in Easthaven as an offering to Auril . His crime, according to Captain Imdra Arlaggath , was murdering the folk of Ten-Towns who had been hired to aid his travels. That was not the end of him. Party Interactions The party met him at Trail's End Tavern , where he gave them the Lantern of Tracking and thirty gold for information on Chwingas . Yin Shen watched him burn in the town square the following day, and the party inherited his scorched Gray Bag of Tricks and a scroll of fireball as a reward from Imdra. One member of his expedition survived: Randy Grailden , who sold the party a map to Dzaan's tower. The Simulacrum What the party found at the bottom of the black spire was Dzaan again, shimmering at the edges like heat-haze. "Ahh! Visitors! I am Dzaan... or almost." He was a simulacrum — incomplete, unstable, and cut off from the original wizard's memories from the moment of his creation. He claimed no knowledge of the execution or the crimes attached to his name. In exchange for an amulet and everything he knew about chardalyn, the party worked an ancient Netherese device that made him fully corporeal. He traveled with them afterward as "Gustavo" : shaved clean, hair cropped short, hat confiscated, and his red scarf dyed blue by Yin Shen. "Why did it have to be blue..." He barely slept, reconstructing his spellbook from memory whenever a sled or wagon stopped jolting enough to write. He promised to teach Yin Shen magic. Flight and Return On a cold night camped short of the Sea of Moving Ice, Dzaan lurched upright from his bedroll and carved a teleportation circle freehand into the snow, talking in a tangle — Red Wizards of Thay , here in Ten-Towns, looking for him. If they found him alongside the party, the party became a problem they would also need to solve, and he would not allow that. He pressed a handwritten folio of magic into Yin Shen's hands, tried to smile, and vanished in blue-white light. He returned after the ceremorphs' ship left the valley — blue, translucent, the landscape visible through him. He was astonished to hear the dragon was dead. Then he told them what he had been doing in Icewind Dale all along: a Netherese city, Ythryn , lies buried in the Reghed Glacier. Auril's magic guards the ice, and neither fire nor pick will open it. The Codicil of White , on Auril's island out in the Sea of Moving Ice, holds an incantation that will. He wants the party to find it — and to recover Professor Skant , his stolen professor orb and an expert on the Netherese Empire. The payoff is the city itself and whatever magic is still lying in it. Canon inconsistency Dzaan names two different pursuers in two different sessions. In Session 20 he is fleeing the Red Wizards of Thay ; in Session 27 he is dodging the Arcane Brotherhood . Both appear in the published story as written and are recorded here unreconciled.

docs.text: Edgra Dermoot Human, Town Speaker of Dougan's Hole An old trapper woman, and the only speaker standing between the Chardalyn Dragon and two towns. When the party worked out the dragon's route from the stone map in Sunblight Fortress — Dougan's Hole, then Goodmead , then Easthaven , eight hours out — Goodmead had no speaker to warn. The seat had sat empty since the last one died in a verbeeg incursion. That left Edgra. Hobbins cast sending while Aronious carried her at a run toward the dogsled: a dragon is coming, eight hours, get to Easthaven, and bring Goodmead's people with you. The answer was curt. Dougan's Hole was leaving its houses where they stood. She did it. Around a hundred and fifty people from the two towns reached Easthaven's gate ahead of the party, carrying what they could. Smoke stood in the sky from the direction of Goodmead.
docs.title: Edgra Dermoot

docs.text: Finkle Shortfuse Gnome, Instrument Merchant — an alias of Polard Hinscrop A small, if enigmatic, gnome merchant located in Easthaven , owner of Strings and Sundries , specialist in wood and string instruments, and for a long while the senior partner in a small musical enterprise with his cousin Hansel Wiresnap . What one didn't sell, the other had on hand. Finkle does not exist. He is Polard Hinscrop in a red shirt. The party unravelled it by carrying him bodily from one shop to the other while he was still insisting he was two people. Cornered, he confessed the whole arrangement. Finkle was retired shortly afterward — "sold" the shop to his brother and left town for warmer lands in the south, which is to say he stopped wearing the red shirt. Aronious was genuinely saddened by the farewell. He came out of retirement once, in the back room of the Musical Empolardium, when the party asked Polard after his brother one time too many. see Music Shop Conspiracy for further reading

docs.text: Foreman Lancastor Human, Miners Guild Foreman of Termalaine Broad shouldered man with a gravely voice and a no nonsense attitude. Leader of the local miners guild and cares deeply for the men he commands. The Lost Miners The party found him behind his desk in the mining offices after reading the notice on the Gelp board: Miners Lost! 50g Reward. The guild had refused all work until the men were found and the mine declared safe. He laid it out without ceremony. Miners were missing, kobolds had moved in, and no one on his crew was going back down until something was done about it. What came back out of the mine was not what he expected. Yin Shen had freed the kobolds from the ghost that had been steering them into banditry and offered them a deal — work the mines for Termalaine free of charge, in exchange for meals and lodging in town. Lancastor looked at the three of them for a long time, then said he needed to check with the Speaker first and left the room with the expression of a man buying himself time to think. He came back with Oarus Masthew , who took the deal.

docs.text: Grandolpha Muzgardt Duergar matron, paramour of Xardorok Sunblight Old in the way that certain things are old — not diminished by it, but concentrated. Long black hair shot through with ribbons of white falls past her shoulders, and her fingernails curve like shards of dark iron. The party found her behind a door in the western hallway of Sunblight Fortress , seated before a hearty buffet of cooked meats, mushrooms, and stranger fare from deeper places that none of them cared to identify. She looked up, assessed them in a single sweep, and gestured to the empty chairs at her table. Her guards received a different signal: weapons away, back to cooking. Hobbins ate one bite of something in the spirit of diplomacy, excused herself from the room with as much dignity as the situation allowed, and returned somewhat paler. Her Position She introduced herself as Xardorok's paramour without embarrassment, and what followed explained why. She had no allegiance to him worth the name. For some time she had been working from within his command, quietly pulling Duergar loyalties toward herself and away from his ambitions. Her intention, once the ground was ready, was to withdraw entirely — to take her people back into the Underdark and breathe life into the failing realm Xardorok had abandoned when the surface offered him grander dreams. She was not an ally by any warm definition of the word. But her interests and theirs pointed, for the moment, in the same direction. The Arrangement She agreed to a shift change. Her men escorted the party down through a service elevator and into the lower stronghold as though they belonged there, navigating around Xardorok's own throne room guards with the practiced ease of people accustomed to working inside a command structure while quietly subverting it. That escort took the party through the main forge and on to the prison cells, where they found Captain Imdra Arlaggath . In the battle, her Duergar repositioned alongside the chanting circle holding the dragon's runic bonds, and took up the chant themselves when Hobbins killed the chanters — fingers finding the links, voices stumbling into a pattern dead men had left unfinished. When the dragon broke free and flew north, Grandolpha's Duergar were left holding chains that no longer bound anything. Afterward Steel was still meeting steel beyond the walls as the party left — the sound of a fortress deciding who it belonged to, now that Xardorok lay dead beside his lever. Grandolpha offered no comment on it. In the party's presence she did nothing at all. Nobody stayed to learn how it came out.

docs.text: Granny Maud Sea hag (deceased) The name the thing in the caves beneath Lac Dinneshere gave itself. The party found her on a gravelly shore by the frozen underground river, humming as she worked — a rusty cleaver rising and falling with a dull wet rhythm against a cutting board, a mound of mangled flesh sorted into grotesque piles before her, and a cauldron bubbling with something thick and foul behind. She turned, lips peeling into a sneer. "Ahh, visitors. Let Granny Maud prepare you some dinner." She was the killer of Easthaven 's missing fishermen. Death Aronious 's bow came up at once, Hobbins hurled spells across the beach, and Yin Shen swept in from the shadows. Under the combined assault the old woman's form split apart like shedding skin, and what emerged was no mortal crone but a towering, blue-skinned sea hag , twisted and wild with hunger. The sight froze Hobbins where she stood. Aronious and Yin Shen broke the spell with sheer ferocity, and the hag collapsed into the gravel. Yin Shen severed the head afterward as proof for the folk of Easthaven. What She Left From her shrivelled hand rolled a small orb glimmering blue in the dim cave light. All three reached for it at once; only Hobbins closed her paw around it. The Sea Hag's Frozen Eye .

docs.text: Henry Davis Guard stationed at The Caer . Member of the Knights of the Black Sword , and by the party's reckoning the lowest-ranking one in the building. Party Interactions Hobbins cast charm person on him from the foot of the castle wall, and Henry — suddenly certain these travelers were trustworthy friends — talked his captain into opening the great doors. He led the party through the cold stone corridors to the Speaker's empty office, admitted he had no idea where the Speaker actually was, and suggested they speak with the soothsayer Hethyl Arkorran . He was still standing too close to the strangers, still smiling, when the captain arrived to find Hethyl dead on the floor. "Restrain them. And clap that traitor in irons." Unresolved The party escaped the Caer. Henry did not go with them, and nothing in the record since says what became of him.

docs.text: Hobbins A ferret wizard who called the frozen north home. Constantly battling against the curiosity she felt looking out at the world from her little shop. Enough was enough — she saw the sky turn dark and a star fall from the heavens. It was time she finally went out there and lived a little. Two and a half feet of white ferret, ten pounds, blue-eyed, nineteen years old, and in possession of an Intelligence score that embarrasses most of the people she meets. Before the Dale Hobbins was born in Goodmead to the well-known Hobbins family, owners of The Magikal Morgue . Despite the name the business is perfectly legitimate, if unsettling to first-time visitors: the family buys magical items recovered from the frozen wastes — salvaged from unlucky adventurers, or sold on by the rare survivors who make it back — then catalogues them, restores what can be restored, and sells to collectors, travellers, and the next crop of hopefuls. Her mother, Logely Hobbins , handles the books and the negotiations with sharp precision. Her father, Drumly Hobbins , has an uncanny eye for an authentic relic. Between them they built a small fortune and one of Goodmead's more prosperous households. She grew up among enchanted trinkets, cursed curiosities, and stories of impossible adventures, and loved all of it — along with the part her parents never quite understood: the thrill of doing the right thing in the most inconvenient and ridiculous way available. If somebody needed help, Hobbins was the sort to sneak out after curfew, steal back a stolen relic, and leave behind a glittering illusion of a goose in a crown purely to confuse the culprit. Her parents consider adventuring a terrible investment. In their view adventurers are future customers, or else future inventory. They had watched too many promising people throw away a future chasing treasure and come back broke, or not come back. Waterdeep Recognising her talent, they sent her to the magical academies of Waterdeep , expecting a respected scholar, enchanter, or merchant who could expand the family business well beyond Icewind Dale. It did not take. For the first time she was surrounded by ambitious wizards, dangerous experiments, and libraries holding knowledge nobody in Goodmead had dreamed of. She excelled — and built a reputation for relentless, harmless mischief. Illusions, disappearing books, enchanted ink. If a professor was cruel, their lecture notes were liable to be ruined by accident. If a classmate was being bullied, they were liable to find a helpful charm in their pocket and a perfectly timed distraction going off across the room. She learned Dwarvish during school breaks, little by little, from a dwarf janitor at the academy. The two of them taught each other things between chores. The more she learned, the more the quiet life her parents had planned felt like a cage. Every ancient spell pointed at forgotten ruins; every professor spoke of discoveries waiting past the edge of civilization. Adventure stopped sounding reckless and started sounding necessary — not for glory, but because there were too many people who needed help, too many secrets under the snow, and far too many rules in the way of doing right by either. The Argument She Is Still Having She left home on good terms, but not happy ones. Her parents never truly approved, and every letter from home still politely encourages her to come to her senses and return to the family business before the Dale claims another fool. What she wants is to prove that adventure is more than greed or recklessness — that knowledge, friendships, and discoveries made past the safety of a shop counter are worth as much as anything sitting on a shelf. More than that, she wants to prove a person can be kind, useful, and wildly inconvenient all at once; that breaking a few rules to help someone is a feature and not a flaw. She would never say it aloud, but every successful expedition feels like another point scored in an argument she has not finished. One day she means to walk back into The Magikal Morgue carrying artifacts no merchant could ever have bought, because nobody else had ever found them. Source Condensed from the player's own text — see Hobbins — Player Backstory . Disposition Hobbins is the party's problem-solver and its single greatest liability, frequently within the same minute. She has talked an awakened plesiosaur out of terrorizing Bremen using nothing but a correct understanding of how awakening works, and she has knocked herself unconscious with her own chromatic orb to win a footrace to a tavern. Her weakness for clear liquor is a running catastrophe. Aronious now pours her measures by the bottle cap. Her family is in Goodmead — six of them in the main household, four of her siblings having moved to the same town. Her father Drumly is among the hopefuls reaching for the empty speaker's seat there. She was also, by Terence Brightbrow 's account and her own, bullied at Waterdeep for being a nerd. She has not forgotten by whom. Deeds Charmed her way past the guards of The Caer and into the Speaker's office. Attuned to the Sea Hag's Frozen Eye by holding it underwater for an hour through a hole Aronious cut in Lac Dinneshere . Broke an avalanche with thunderwave and saved the party from burial. Healed Lupine with her medicine kit while disguised as a dire wolf pup, and received his boon. Rode out a radiant catastrophe inside a chest of temporal stasis, which she then kept. docs.text: A ferret wizard who called the frozen north home. Constantly battling against the curiosity she felt looking out at the world from her little shop. Enough was enough — she saw the sky turn dark and a star fall from the heavens. It was time she finally went out there and lived a little. Two and a half feet of white ferret, ten pounds, blue-eyed, nineteen years old, and in possession of an Intelligence score that embarrasses most of the people she meets.
docs.title: Hobbins

docs.text: Hobbins was born in Goodmead to the well-known Hobbins family, owners of The Magikal Morgue . Despite the name the business is perfectly legitimate, if unsettling to first-time visitors: the family buys magical items recovered from the frozen wastes — salvaged from unlucky adventurers, or sold on by the rare survivors who make it back — then catalogues them, restores what can be restored, and sells to collectors, travellers, and the next crop of hopefuls. Her mother, Logely Hobbins , handles the books and the negotiations with sharp precision. Her father, Drumly Hobbins , has an uncanny eye for an authentic relic. Between them they built a small fortune and one of Goodmead's more prosperous households. She grew up among enchanted trinkets, cursed curiosities, and stories of impossible adventures, and loved all of it — along with the part her parents never quite understood: the thrill of doing the right thing in the most inconvenient and ridiculous way available. If somebody needed help, Hobbins was the sort to sneak out after curfew, steal back a stolen relic, and leave behind a glittering illusion of a goose in a crown purely to confuse the culprit. Her parents consider adventuring a terrible investment. In their view adventurers are future customers, or else future inventory. They had watched too many promising people throw away a future chasing treasure and come back broke, or not come back.
docs.title: Before the Dale

docs.text: Recognising her talent, they sent her to the magical academies of Waterdeep , expecting a respected scholar, enchanter, or merchant who could expand the family business well beyond Icewind Dale. It did not take. For the first time she was surrounded by ambitious wizards, dangerous experiments, and libraries holding knowledge nobody in Goodmead had dreamed of. She excelled — and built a reputation for relentless, harmless mischief. Illusions, disappearing books, enchanted ink. If a professor was cruel, their lecture notes were liable to be ruined by accident. If a classmate was being bullied, they were liable to find a helpful charm in their pocket and a perfectly timed distraction going off across the room. She learned Dwarvish during school breaks, little by little, from a dwarf janitor at the academy. The two of them taught each other things between chores. The more she learned, the more the quiet life her parents had planned felt like a cage. Every ancient spell pointed at forgotten ruins; every professor spoke of discoveries waiting past the edge of civilization. Adventure stopped sounding reckless and started sounding necessary — not for glory, but because there were too many people who needed help, too many secrets under the snow, and far too many rules in the way of doing right by either.
docs.title: Waterdeep

docs.text: She left home on good terms, but not happy ones. Her parents never truly approved, and every letter from home still politely encourages her to come to her senses and return to the family business before the Dale claims another fool. What she wants is to prove that adventure is more than greed or recklessness — that knowledge, friendships, and discoveries made past the safety of a shop counter are worth as much as anything sitting on a shelf. More than that, she wants to prove a person can be kind, useful, and wildly inconvenient all at once; that breaking a few rules to help someone is a feature and not a flaw. She would never say it aloud, but every successful expedition feels like another point scored in an argument she has not finished. One day she means to walk back into The Magikal Morgue carrying artifacts no merchant could ever have bought, because nobody else had ever found them. Source Condensed from the player's own text — see Hobbins — Player Backstory .
docs.title: The Argument She Is Still Having

docs.text: Hobbins is the party's problem-solver and its single greatest liability, frequently within the same minute. She has talked an awakened plesiosaur out of terrorizing Bremen using nothing but a correct understanding of how awakening works, and she has knocked herself unconscious with her own chromatic orb to win a footrace to a tavern. Her weakness for clear liquor is a running catastrophe. Aronious now pours her measures by the bottle cap. Her family is in Goodmead — six of them in the main household, four of her siblings having moved to the same town. Her father Drumly is among the hopefuls reaching for the empty speaker's seat there. She was also, by Terence Brightbrow 's account and her own, bullied at Waterdeep for being a nerd. She has not forgotten by whom.

docs.text: Karthax Dragonborn, Armorer of Termalaine The armorer in Termalaine . Yin Shen brought him the tentacles cut from the grell killed in the town's mines and laid them on his workbench. He turned them over, considered the tensile quality of the tissue, and told her to return in the morning. He had the work done by then: the tentacles cured and lashed with leather bindings into a serviceable Grell Tentacle Whip . Yin Shen took it without ceremony and has carried it since.

docs.text: Krintas Undead attendant The undead companion of Dzaan 's simulacrum at The Black Spire . Yin Shen first heard him through a wall, being muttered at over parchment about failed experiments and a missing lifespark. He accompanied the party and Dzaan down to the chamber of the Netherese machine. When the vortex destabilised, Krintas shoved the party out of the chamber — and took the worst of the radiant blast himself, hurled into a wall with his flesh scorched and smouldering. He left the spire with Dzaan when the simulacrum agreed to travel with the party.

docs.text: Lupine Awakened Dire Wolf, godling — see Godlings and Divine Energy A powerful and divine creature holding a domain in the eastern wilderness of Icewind Dale . The party first encountered him in a cave he used for shelter, gravely wounded — his flanks torn open, blue wisps rising from his form — after a confrontation with Ursa , a polar bear godling who had grown discontent with the borders of her own realm and attacked him to consume his. Hobbins approached disguised as a dire wolf pup and tended his wounds with her medicine kit while Aronious spoke the words of speak with animals , and understanding bloomed between them. "I am Lupine. Once a dire wolf. Now... something more." He forbade them from hunting Ursa — "She is far beyond you" — and set them a different test: Skree , a deranged awakened bat whose chaos threatened the balance the godlings keep. "Skree is a deranged godling. Ursa is merely an ambitious cub. One must fall before the other can be faced." Friendship, Not Company The party killed Skree and returned with his collar and the corrupt totem they found in his cave. Lupine's wounds had healed. Yin Shen asked him to travel with them, and he refused. "I am needed here. My domain requires me. But know this — you have proven yourselves, and you have earned my friendship. Should you face a threat too great to bear alone, call upon me. I will come." Then he rose to his full height, a blue glow rising off him, and had the party hold their weapons aloft. Frozen air poured from his maw and settled on the steel and wood as delicate ice crystals before fading into them. Both Hobbins and Yin Shen carry the result on their sheets as Lupine's Boon — a gift of the dire wolf demigod, +1 to hit and +1 to damage. His name still carries weight in the Dale. When the party needed an ancient white dragon to take a sending seriously, the message they chose to send was that Lupine can vouch . Ursa remains unfaced.

docs.text: Mylbor Tarrfak Dwarf, Trophy Hunter A barrel-chested trophy hunter with a cabin northeast of Bremen , trailing a long red beard packed with snow. Encountered by the party during a blizzard while hunting a dangerous Red Yeti as a field test for his homemade "Thunder Stick" — a crude, single-shot blunderbuss of his own design, uncommon enough that the party did not recognize it on sight. Boisterous and eager for a worthy quarry. He proposed a wager of 300 gold that he could find the Yeti before the party, which they declined. When Yin Shen raised the prospect of hunting the Chardalyn Dragon, his interest was lukewarm until she mentioned the involvement of Duergar — at which point ancestral fury made the decision for him. "That certainly sweetens the deal." The Yeti and the Cask He made the Bremen tavern two days later as promised, kicking the door open with a crimson-stained sack over one shoulder and the Thunder Stick in his other hand — or what was left of it, the end mushroomed outward into a tangle of singed and curling metal. "Only took one shot. Though I only had one shot." He threw his purse on the bar, bought a round, and looked around the table with the expectant expression of a man waiting to be matched. Aronious poured a full bottle of clear liquor down without pause. The barmaid put that at a cask of ale; Mylbor was behind the bar and on the floor before anyone thought to stop him, and tapped out partway through with great reluctance. "You win, laddy." He and Yin Shen agreed over breakfast to stay in contact — she wanted word of the ancient white dragon, he wanted word of anything worth hunting. The Fortress He answered Hobbins' sending about a Duergar stronghold in the same register he answers everything, immediately and enthusiastically, and arrived at the Termalaine inn that evening by kicking the door open. He fought through the entrance hall of Xardorok Sunblight's fortress — hemmed in and unable to bring his weight to bear in the narrow space — then cut through the throne room alongside Polard and the Shield Guardian to open the forge from the far end, raising what remained of the Thunder Stick and wading in.

docs.text: Oarus Masthew Orc, Town Speaker of Termalaine A large, broad-shouldered orc who carries the authority of his office the way most men carry a weapon — visibly, and without apparent effort. He dresses in fine clothing that sits oddly at odds with the rough work he seems most comfortable doing, and is rarely found behind a desk when there is something more immediate to be attended to. When Captain Imdra Arlaggath sent word of the Duergar incursion and the threat gathering beneath the mountains, Masthew did not wait for further instruction. He pulled every able-bodied person in Termalaine who could hold a weapon and began drilling them in the street. Most had never seen combat. He appears unconcerned by this, reasoning that inexperienced soldiers are better than no soldiers, and that experience is simply something you survive long enough to acquire. He received the party warmly upon learning they operated under Imdra's authority, asked no unnecessary questions, and returned immediately to his militia. He strikes the party as a man who finds comfort in action and tends to trust people who demonstrate the same. The Kobold Arrangement When Foreman Lancastor brought him three kobolds standing in a trenchcoat of blanket, Masthew looked at the kobolds, looked at the party, and formally accepted the arrangement on behalf of Termalaine without visible hesitation: food and shelter in exchange for work in the mines. His militia drilling had already paid off. Termalaine repelled its own Duergar incursion and captured one of the attackers, who gave up the location of the stronghold in the Spine of the World under questioning. It was Masthew who told the party that Easthaven had been hit and that Imdra had been taken.

docs.text: Polard Hinscrop Gnome, Instrument Merchant and Adventurer (retired) The gnome behind both halves of the Music Shop Conspiracy — proprietor of Strings and Sundries , proprietor of Drums Emporium , and sole performer of the roles of "Finkle Shortfuse" and "Hansel Wiresnap." He is embarrassed by his real name, which he considers distinctly un-gnomish, and gave it up only under pressure. Hobbins gave him the business advice that saved him, and he has treated her as a mentor ever since. Adventuring Career After merging his two shops under "new management," Polard took up Aronious 's invitation and joined the party, arriving in a suit of armor he had made himself: a metal pasta strainer for a helmet, bent cymbals for shoulder pads, and a hodgepodge of kitchen utensils, instrument parts, and leather straps for the rest. The dwarven smiths of Easthaven inspected it, laughed, and then admitted the craftsmanship was genuinely good and that it would stop a blade. At the goblin stronghold, with arrows falling on his companions, something in him turned over. "Not at my friends!" Every seam of the armor sealed and melted flush, the whole of it fusing into one immaculate piece — and then growing, swelling to ten feet tall as a deep resonant voice rolled out from inside it. A lightning hammer ignited in his fist. He has fought that way since, at the burning stronghold and again in the entrance hall and throne room of Xardorok Sunblight's fortress. Retirement The Chardalyn Dragon's radiant breath went straight down Polard's lane in Easthaven and left nothing standing. He went to his knees in the rubble and wept. When Hobbins asked whether the shop had been insured, he produced the pamphlet, turned to the last page, and showed them the final unchecked box. "I never got it notarized." A week later the town had doubled his plot in thanks for his part in the defense. He told the party he was stepping back from adventuring — a hiatus, a temporary retirement, as he put it — and meant to install a forge and train with the Easthaven blacksmith so that he could supply the party's gear himself. He cried as they left, and asked them to visit often. The rebuilt shop is larger than the old one and about half finished. He has hired an assistant named Samantha. At the party's suggestion he renamed it the Musical Empolardium , and did not need to think about it: "Samantha, we need to change the sign immediately." Asked again after his brother, he hesitated, stepped into the back room, and came out in a different shirt as Finkle Shortfuse. Aronious caught the flicker of confusion and accepted the brother anyway. docs.text: Gnome, Instrument Merchant and Adventurer (retired) The gnome behind both halves of the Music Shop Conspiracy — proprietor of Strings and Sundries , proprietor of Drums Emporium , and sole performer of the roles of "Finkle Shortfuse" and "Hansel Wiresnap." He is embarrassed by his real name, which he considers distinctly un-gnomish, and gave it up only under pressure. Hobbins gave him the business advice that saved him, and he has treated her as a mentor ever since.
docs.title: Polard Hinscrop

docs.text: After merging his two shops under "new management," Polard took up Aronious 's invitation and joined the party, arriving in a suit of armor he had made himself: a metal pasta strainer for a helmet, bent cymbals for shoulder pads, and a hodgepodge of kitchen utensils, instrument parts, and leather straps for the rest. The dwarven smiths of Easthaven inspected it, laughed, and then admitted the craftsmanship was genuinely good and that it would stop a blade. At the goblin stronghold, with arrows falling on his companions, something in him turned over. "Not at my friends!" Every seam of the armor sealed and melted flush, the whole of it fusing into one immaculate piece — and then growing, swelling to ten feet tall as a deep resonant voice rolled out from inside it. A lightning hammer ignited in his fist. He has fought that way since, at the burning stronghold and again in the entrance hall and throne room of Xardorok Sunblight's fortress.
docs.title: Adventuring Career

docs.text: The Chardalyn Dragon's radiant breath went straight down Polard's lane in Easthaven and left nothing standing. He went to his knees in the rubble and wept. When Hobbins asked whether the shop had been insured, he produced the pamphlet, turned to the last page, and showed them the final unchecked box. "I never got it notarized." A week later the town had doubled his plot in thanks for his part in the defense. He told the party he was stepping back from adventuring — a hiatus, a temporary retirement, as he put it — and meant to install a forge and train with the Easthaven blacksmith so that he could supply the party's gear himself. He cried as they left, and asked them to visit often. The rebuilt shop is larger than the old one and about half finished. He has hired an assistant named Samantha. At the party's suggestion he renamed it the Musical Empolardium , and did not need to think about it: "Samantha, we need to change the sign immediately." Asked again after his brother, he hesitated, stepped into the back room, and came out in a different shirt as Finkle Shortfuse. Aronious caught the flicker of confusion and accepted the brother anyway.
docs.title: Retirement

docs.text: Randy Grailden Human The sole surviving member of the expedition Dzaan took into the wilderness. He made it back alive and alone, and was recovering at The White Lady Inn in Easthaven when Yin Shen found him. He clammed up the moment she asked, hands shaking, and kept eating. "I don't know nothing. He took me, is all." She pressed him until he understood that she knew he had been to the tower, knew he had come back, and knew everyone had a price. He worked his own out loud. "Fifteen gold to get out of this hell hole, and five more to keep me comfy for a short while... yes, yes, that should do." He asked for twenty. She paid without hesitation, and he sketched the route to Dzaan's tower onto her map with a trembling hand. That map led the party to the black spire — and to what was waiting at the bottom of it.
docs.title: Randy Grailden

docs.text: Rinaldo Bard, The White Lady Inn A self-styled bard of quick fingers and quicker tongue, kept around the White Lady Inn in Easthaven to entertain guests. He is fond of plucking his fiddle while recounting the legend the inn is named for — the White Lady, a ghost said to walk on Lac Dinneshere where her rich husband drowned, a miser who kept his treasure in a heavy locked chest that never left his side. The Séance He announced he would hold a séance to summon her. Yin Shen attended out of curiosity; Aronious stayed upstairs, wary of dealings with spirits. The candles dimmed and Rinaldo began, voice weaving through false prayers and soft illusions. Then the air shifted — colder, and real. The candles guttered. A thin wisp of silver smoke coiled up from the centre of the room and formed the faint outline of a woman's face. " Caer-Dineval . " Then she was gone. Rinaldo went pale and trembling and ushered the guests out at once. Yin Shen lingered, and a single glance from her foxlike eyes drew the truth out of him: his séances had always been performances , harmless illusions meant to entertain. This time, what he summoned answered him. That one word sent the party to Caer-Dineval, to the Knights of the Black Sword and the dying prophecy of Hethyl Arkorran . The White Lady has not spoken since. Yin Shen searched the lakeshore the following morning and found nothing.

docs.text: Sephek Kaltro A blue-eyed killer who traveled with Torg's Trading Company as a caravan guard, stalked across Ten-Towns by Hiln Trollbane and said to serve some darker purpose beneath the Frostmaiden's will. Party Interactions The party tracked him from Trail's End Tavern through a blizzard, following footprints out of an open window and into a forest glade. They found him there in the moonlight with his blade drawn above a trembling Chwinga . He fought with inhuman grace, struck down Aronious , and died with the light going out of his eyes. His body melted into the snow, leaving only his blade. The Dagger The weapon shattered as he fell — and then drew itself back together, the shards fusing into a dagger whose edge carries an eerie black anti-glow, as if even the darkness feared to touch it. Yin Shen reached for it. It burned cold in her palm and did her no harm. It pulsed once, as if recognizing her fallen divinity, and then fell silent.

docs.text: Shuāng Celestial, servant of Tyr — twin sister of Yin Shen The other half of the pair. Where Yin Shen went into the shadows, Shuāng stood in the open in heavy, deliberately loud armor and drew every eye in the room. She is a devoted follower of Tyr and defended the celestial realm against the evil spirits that threatened it, which she did gladly. Her weapon is the Dragon's Glaive , its blade coated in a purifying flame no evil spirit survives — and which doubles, usefully, as a lie detector. Side by side the twins were close to unbeatable. Shuāng took the attention and the front of the fight; Yin Shen came in silent from behind with the black lotus sword . Temperament Shuāng was the one who carried out Yin Shen's punishments — the language drills, the fragile objects to be cleaned, the inventories to be catalogued, the letters of apology, the full days spent stuck in fox form. She found her sister exhausting. She also privately admired how creative the pranks could get, and would never have said so out loud. At the end of it they were family, and they cared for each other. Her own time went to writing poetry, practising her techniques and her flute, trying new kinds of tea, meditating, and — occasionally — eating sweets. The Exile When the festival ended in fire and bodies, it was Shuāng who carried word of it to Tyr. She is a servant of justice and she behaved like one. The party's record names her plainly as "the one who had brought about her exile." At the trial Yin Shen could bear the gods refusing to listen. What she could not bear was her own sister — the one who had put her in front of that court — unable to look in her direction. She did not want her family believing she had some twisted dark side to her. The last thing she saw as Tyr cast her down was her family crying. She does not know whether they wept because she was banished or because they thought she was a monster. Whether Shuāng expected Tyr to go as far as he did is not recorded. She did not speak for her. Since Yin Shen prayed to her in an alley in Easthaven on the night the Chardalyn Dragon came, for the first time since the fall. Snow began to fall. A golden, pale face that was not Yin Shen's own looked back out of a frozen puddle, and the sigil of Tyr melted itself into the ice. No weapon came and no spell, but she had been heard. Yin Shen offered a prayer of thanks when the dragon was dead.

docs.text: Skree Awakened Giant Bat, godling (deceased) A corrupted divine creature who dwelt in a small cave complex in the mountains southeast of Easthaven . Lupine named him a danger to all who wandered near and set him as the party's proof of worth. He was a horror to look at by the end. His once-sleek fur was matted and torn, his body riddled with pustules and rot, wounds weeping across his wings and flanks — and a wrongness radiated off him that went deeper than madness. Death The party reached him through a spider den, past hundreds of bats spiralling through the dark. Hobbins had chosen her spells for the fight, hurling thunderous orbs that struck at his keen and fragile senses, while Aronious 's dire wolf tore bats from the air and Yin Shen thinned the swarm from the shadows. A sonic pulse from Skree shook the cave and dropped Aronious where he stood. Hobbins and Yin Shen doubled their assault, and the godling fell from the air to the stone below. Hobbins recovered Skree's Collar and his charm from the body as proof for Lupine. The Corruption The wrongness did not die with him. The party followed it to a shadowed alcove and found a dark totem radiating the same foul energy that had poisoned him — see the Off-putting Effigy . See also Godlings and Divine Energy . Hobbins wrapped it in cloth to dull its influence and carried it out. Whatever corrupted Skree was not Skree's own doing, and its source has not been found.

docs.text: Soppo Ice mephit, self-appointed guide to Auril's Island A small ice mephit that was on the shattered giants' dock waving and jabbering as the party's longboat came in, riding low with the Shield Guardian aboard. It speaks Auran . Hobbins cast comprehend languages as a ritual and has done the talking ever since, passing along what comes back. Soppo offered to be their guide. There is plenty to see, by its account: shipwrecks full of goods, a field of ice sculptures, and a recent wreck with one survivor who made it as far as the shore and froze there. "Soppo hasn't had visitors in a while. Again, unless you count the one who crawled ashore, though she didn't last." Asked about Professor Skant , it did not know the orb. Asked about the Codicil of White , it looked shocked, and called it the lady's book . That is at Grimskalle , at the centre of the island, where it is dangerous. The tour it proposed runs fourteen hours with Grimskalle at the end. The party accepted. Yin Shen kept her guard up.

docs.text: Spellix Romwood Gnome, Merchant A gnome merchant whose caravan was ambushed by goblins in the mountain pass entrance to Icewind Dale , losing his goods and companions in the raid. In a desperate attempt to free his people, he fashioned a goblin disguise — only to accidentally stumble into the role of goblin chief, through a series of events he described as "immediately going wrong in every direction." He remained trapped in the role, certain that goblin elders had seen through his ruse and were plotting against him. He revealed himself to the party in a room he called the "chatting chamber," by closing the door and pulling his own head off. Rescued during their raid on the goblin stronghold, he fled the burning fortress alongside them and escaped to Bremen . He thanked them with genuine warmth, explained he would be staying at the inn briefly before heading south to his family, then turned out his pockets to reveal they were entirely empty and shrugged — perhaps the inn was too much to hope for. Aronious pressed two gold into his hand without a word.

docs.text: Terence Brightbrow Gnome Wizard, party boy of the university in Waterdeep A gnome in the same robe and the same hat as Hobbins , working a room with finger guns that shoot confetti, balloons, and mage hands. He hosts a speakeasy beneath a disused dog sled kennel in Easthaven — an empty shack fifteen feet across with a hatch in the floor, and beneath the hatch a metal spiral staircase winding down into a cavern that has no business fitting under it, packed with partygoers from more regions than Easthaven sees in a year. Hobbins knew him. He was the party boy of the university in Waterdeep, and he bullied her for being a nerd. He denied it. "Hey, don't try and harsh my mellow. I'm here for a party for everybody." Then his finger slipped, and a streamer unfurled across the room reading no nerds allowed . He bought the room a round, and every eye in the cavern began to glow blue. Hobbins left on friendly terms with a bottle of the same white liquor under her arm, telling him that if he wanted to find her he could ask the townsfolk. What He Is Actually Capable Of Six Easthaven guards raided the shack above over unpaid taxes, carrying cudgels only. Hobbins hid in a hay-filled box and watched through the slats: the out-of-town guests left by portal, and the guards came back up with nothing but Easthaven locals and no explanation for why the place had been bigger a moment before. When they were gone she went back down. The staircase ended in the kennel's cold-storage cellar — frozen, small, and entirely ordinary. Hobbins put it at something like mighty fortress . Eighth-level conjuration. From a man whose reputation does not reach anywhere near it.
docs.title: Terence Brightbrow

Then his finger slipped, and a streamer unfurled across the room reading no nerds allowed . He bought the room a round, and every eye in the cavern began to glow blue. Hobbins left on friendly terms with a bottle of the same white liquor under her arm, telling him that if he wanted to find her he could ask the townsfolk.
docs.title: Terence Brightbrow

docs.text: Six Easthaven guards raided the shack above over unpaid taxes, carrying cudgels only. Hobbins hid in a hay-filled box and watched through the slats: the out-of-town guests left by portal, and the guards came back up with nothing but Easthaven locals and no explanation for why the place had been bigger a moment before. When they were gone she went back down. The staircase ended in the kennel's cold-storage cellar — frozen, small, and entirely ordinary. Hobbins put it at something like mighty fortress . Eighth-level conjuration. From a man whose reputation does not reach anywhere near it.
docs.title: What He Is Actually Capable Of

docs.text: Tinjong Verbeeg, Servant of Sylvanas A nine-foot-tall giant in thick walrus hide armor bounds across the ice with surprising speed and grace despite her gangly, misshapen limbs. Although her narrow face is hard to see under the fur-lined hood of her frost-covered cloak, it's clear that the left side of her face sags much lower than the right. She fills her cave the way certain people fill a room — not through effort, but through simple fact of presence. The Rescue The party met her in the fog outside a shipwreck on the Sea of Moving Ice , with an ancient white dragon's head pushing in through the breach behind them. "I think you could use some help." A fog cloud rolled through the hold in a single dense surge. "To me!" She was already shouldering her club and shield into carry position when they reached her, and did not wait for introductions. "Quick. My cave." They ran. The dragon answered its own anger with a blast of breath aimed at the sky, and spears of ice came down like thrown lances the whole way. Tinjong set her club and shield against the cave wall afterward with the unhurried manner of someone returning from an unremarkable errand. As she straightened, a Chwinga emerged from behind a low rock shelf, its face marked with a pattern the party found immediately and inexplicably familiar. She extended her little finger and the creature touched it gently — a greeting between two beings who had clearly known each other a long time. Where She Stands Tinjong is a servant of Sylvanas , god of nature. She was plain about the limits of that: the fight between Ten-Towns and the Duergar is not her concern, and she made no apology for it. The Rime is another matter. An endless, unnatural winter pressed against the grain of the world itself is exactly her concern, and anything that moves against Auril can count on her when the time comes. Aronious spent some time in quiet conversation with her before the party left — the particular kind of exchange that passes between two people who understand the wild and are not in a hurry.

docs.text: Torvus Silver Dragonborn, Town Speaker The Town Speaker for Caer-Konig , and — by his own appointment — its lead investigator. A known drunk who does not mind being a silver dragonborn half-frozen in a snowdrift, and who is regularly brought in from "patrol" by Cori and Allie to be fed something warm. He introduced himself to the party by erupting out of a snowbank and swinging drunkenly for Yin Shen 's wrist. "Who goes there? Is it thieves? Have I found those creeping bastards?" He had been hunting the town's petty thieves for some time without result, most recently the magic lantern stolen from The Northern Light , and regaled the party with tales of his adventuring days and how his experience made him perfectly suited to the role. The Writ When the party returned the lantern along with a bound Duergar prisoner and the story of a frozen stronghold, Torvus was genuinely shaken. "And here I thought I was looking for petty thieves." Asked whether he would speak to the other town speakers, he did better. Despite the drink his hand was steady and his words clear. He drafted a legal document deputizing the party as agents of Caer-Konig , reporting directly to the town Speaker, and rolled his signet ring into the wax seal. "This should go a long way in proving you've got our backing." Then he emptied his pockets onto the counter — four separate half-empty containers of alcohol came out first — and produced a Torg's Trading Company travel voucher , valid for Eastway travel but not servicing Lonelywood or Dougan's Hole. "It's no silver bullet, but it'll get you across Ten-Towns no problem." That writ, endorsed afterward by Captain Imdra Arlaggath , is the legal basis for everything the party has done in Ten-Towns since.

docs.text: Ursa Awakened polar bear, godling A godling who has grown discontent with the borders of her realm, and the reason Lupine was lying torn open in a cave when the party found him. She attacked him seeking to consume his domain and claim his power for herself . The fight nearly killed him; his flanks were still oozing into matted grey fur days later, and blue wisps rose off him as he licked at the wounds. Aronious offered to hunt her. Lupine's eyes flared with something close to panic. "No. Do not seek her out alone. She is far beyond you." He set them on Skree instead, and was explicit about the order of things: "Skree is a deranged godling. Ursa is merely an ambitious cub. One must fall before the other can be faced." Skree has fallen. Lupine's wounds have healed and his domain holds for now. Ursa remains unfaced. See Godlings and Divine Energy .

docs.text: Voren Ceremorph, gnome-sized One of the ceremorphs aboard the crashed nautiloid in the far north, and the one who did the talking. Hobbins heard Gnomish through a door on the middle deck, knocked, and went in alone. Voren was repairing the ship. He explained it had been a research mission: they collected creatures, two carrion crawlers and a larger beast that tunnels. After the crash there was no way to feed them, so they let all three go — which accounts for the things that came up out of the snow and dragged Yin Shen toward the hull. They answer, he said, to something called the mother brain . He insisted they were not controlled, not the way other mind flayers are. Then his scanner found a power source on the other side of the wall, which was where Yin Shen was standing. "The visitors on the ship, yes, they might be able to help. I sure hope our golem hasn't done any damage to them." Asked whether he would come to the party's aid if called by sending : "No, I don't think we can do that. We gotta get out of here. We've already caused too much trouble being stuck in this area. If someone discovers us, they'll definitely take us down." The Trade When Yin Shen came in with the psi crystal she had taken from a mind flayer's skull in the Termalaine mines, Voren stopped using his mouth and spoke inside their heads instead. He named the crystal, and showed them the one burnt out in the ship's propulsion. He refused to trade future transport. An item he would do. Dredavex produced a small chitinous chest holding a pair of crystal lenses and an owl-shaped helmet capped with something very like a brain — later identified as Eyes of Minute Seeing and a Helm of Telepathy . The ceremorphs were not upset about the golem the party had destroyed. They would rather get off the planet than dwell on it. Departure Voren was plain about the rest. They were bound for the Astral realm . The party could not come, and after that he did not expect anyone would be able to reach them. The tentacles tore free, the ship rose, and then it was a streak in the sky, and then it wasn't.

docs.text: Xardorok Sunblight Duergar, Lord of Clan Sunblight (deceased) The Duergar lord whose ambition drove the whole of the chardalyn conspiracy. He abandoned a failing realm in the Underdark for grander dreams of conquest on the surface, and spent them building one weapon. He was first known to the party only as a boast. A Duergar in finery, pinned in a spike trap beneath Kelvin's Cairn , bellowed in Dwarvish: My father is more powerful than any of you filthy creatures could imagine! You don't understand the glory of it, the power found in the ice. None of you do. But you will learn soon enough when my father unleashes his terror upon Ten-Towns! Your doom soars on dragon's wings! The soothsayer Hethyl Arkorran had already seen it, years out and wrapped in prophecy: a fortress, a villain, a crystal machine with a dragon's heart. The Forge The party found him at last in Sunblight Fortress , on a raised platform above his main forge — a pyramid of stone ten feet tall with its apex sheared off, pulsing slow and deep from within like something breathing. Chained beneath an opening in the ceiling, runic links burning against dark crystal hide, was the Chardalyn Dragon , vast and black and furious in the particular way of something powerful that has been made to hold still. He watched his work with the satisfaction of a man who has built something terrible and knows it. A stone relief table in the upper fortress showed what he intended: Ten-Towns carved in miniature, a channel cut between all ten settlements in a continuous loop, and a dragon figurine on an iron pole that a crank walked around the circuit. Someone had been plotting the route for a long time. Death His own paramour betrayed him. Grandolpha Muzgardt had been quietly pulling Duergar loyalties away from him for some time, and it was her escort that walked the party through his forge unchallenged. When the fight came he fought with a black crystal gauntlet that tore the floor open with hellfire from a plane that had no business being involved. He put Yin Shen through the floor with it and dropped Hobbins singed and still to the stone — she came back only because Aronious ran to her and called on Sylvanas. He went invisible. It bought him nothing: Yin Shen had him bound with witch bolt and Aronious had laid hunter's mark on the same thread. He emerged on the far side of the forge and threw a lever set into the wall, bringing ice cascading through the ceiling. He was still pulling it when the party descended on him. He fell beside his lever, alone in the way that men who trade loyalty for power tend to find themselves at the end. His death did not stop the dragon. The chains went slack, the runes failed, and it launched itself up through the hole in the ceiling and north over Icewind Dale. Clan See Clan Sunblight . He had at least two sons. One was interrogated and killed at the Kelvin's Cairn outpost; the other, Durth , wrote to him from a new base on the Easthaven ferry. See Durth and Clan Sunblight .
docs.title: Xardorok Sunblight

docs.text: Yin Shen A former celestial trickster spirit, cast down and held in the frozen north of Icewind Dale. Before the Fall Yin Shen was a lesser god of the celestial heavens — goddess of trickery and mischief, of the kind of trick that is usually harmless. Her family lived under the rule of Tyr , god of justice, though not uniformly: her mother and her sister kept his rule, while her father held that bending a rule was fine so long as nobody got hurt. She was a prodigy of mischief, with an exact sense of which buttons could be pushed and how far. In time she was worshipped for it, by troublemaking children up to no good — and worship made her bolder and her tricks riskier. Her twin sister is Shuāng , a devoted servant of Tyr who defended the celestial realm from the evil spirits that threatened it. The two of them were a matched pair on a battlefield and nearly unbeatable together: Shuāng loud and deliberate in heavy armor, drawing every eye with the Dragon's Glaive ; Yin Shen gone into the shadows and arriving behind the enemy with her black lotus sword , a blade as dark as night and silent as the grave. In her kimono nobody heard her coming, and by the time they did it was already too late. Yin Shen only fought when made to — usually as a punishment. Her other sentences ran to practising languages, studying threats to the realm, cleaning very fragile objects, cataloguing the armoury, writing apologies to the people she had pranked, and being stuck in fox form for a full day. Shuāng generally carried them out. Among the many gods she annoyed, she kept one mortal friend: a paladin named Aronious III , posted to guard her shrine. He was righteous and good and everything she found tiresome about Tyr, and she spent her afternoons needling him, boasting about what she had gotten away with, and trying without success to get him to worship her. The Fall Her mistake was small, and then it was not. At a festival — the night merry, the offerings laid out — she set out to inconvenience her sister and the other gods by blessing a child to interfere with the offerings. He asked to be able to cast a higher tier of fire spells. She assumed a fire dancer, or an evocation mage there to entertain, and she did not look any further into it. By the time she noticed, it was far too late. The night turned from merriment to horror. The offerings were destroyed, the festival ruined, most of the crowd injured, and some of them died . It was nobody's fault but hers, and she has never pretended otherwise. The boy was never punished; the townspeople never learned who had caused it. She remembers his face. It was Shuāng who carried word of the disaster to Tyr. The knock came at her door the next day. She stood before the court and pleaded that she had meant no harm, that it was supposed to be harmless, that no one was supposed to be hurt. The gods would not listen — she could bear that. What she could not bear was that her own sister, the one who had put her there, could not look in her direction. Tyr came down to deliver judgement himself, without bothering to hear her side. He stripped her of her title, her kimono, her magic, her immortality, and her sword. He cast her into Auril 's realm of frost and scattered her possessions across Icewind Dale . The last thing she saw was her family crying. Whether from grief at her banishment or from the belief that she was a monster, she does not know, and may never. Scattered Regalia Tyr did not destroy what he took from her. He scattered it across Icewind Dale , which means it is out there. Black Lotus Sword — unrecovered Yin Shen's Kimono — unrecovered Recovering them, and reconnecting herself to the Weave, is what she has been doing in the Dale since the day she landed in it. The Years in the Dale She nearly did not survive the first stretch. She was desperate, and by her own account came close to giving up; what carried her through was the kindness of strangers in Ten-Towns. After that she survived on what she is best at — sneaking, stealing, pranks, and cheating. Liar's dice, poker, whatever was being played in the bar. She did not play for money; she knew better than to draw attention by taking people's coin where they would notice. She played for information, for food, for necessities. Her winning streak at the bar in Dougan's Hole was notorious and entirely tolerated, on the grounds that she never asked for money when she won. How she got into those games with no coin to her name is a question she has declined to answer. She was a thief and a scoundrel, and also a friendly face who liked bringing people joy. She told stories about her time in the heavens that nobody believed and everybody enjoyed, and she collected the town's gossip in exchange. It still pains her that when children pray to her for help with some small mischief, she has no blessing left to give them. Source Condensed from the player's own text — see Yin Shen — Player Backstory . The Prayer in the Alley On the night the Chardalyn Dragon came for Easthaven , Yin Shen found an alley with no one in it and spoke to her sister Shuāng — the one who had brought about her exile — for the first time since the fall. "I know I fucked up in the past. I don't ask much from you, but please, if you can, help these people out." Snow began to fall. In a frozen puddle the face looking back at her was golden and pale and not her own, there for a moment and then gone, and the sigil of Tyr melted itself into the ice. No weapon came. No spell. But she had been heard, and she walked out of that alley carrying something she had not carried in. She was not the only one to see it: elsewhere in the town, Aronious and Hobbins each caught a glimpse of a figure who looked a great deal like her — one in a shiny rock at the front of the militia, one as a shape among the stars. She offered a prayer of thanks to her sister when the dragon was dead. Deeds Claimed Sephek Kaltro 's reforged dagger, which burned cold in her palm but did not harm her. Melted her way out of the Caer's cistern with kitsune fire and freed five prisoners with her. Bargained twenty gold out of Randy Grailden for the map to the black spire. Caught all four falling phials of a potion chest in mid-air, one-handed, at an uncomfortable angle. Shaved, cropped, and re-dyed Dzaan into "Gustavo" so he could walk into Easthaven without burning twice. Held the rope at the burning goblin stronghold until every one of her companions was down it. Pinned the Chardalyn Dragon's head by driving her shortsword into a vent in its neck. Sold the Sunblight treasure to an Easthaven jeweler without telling anyone, and has still not said what the total was. docs.text: A former celestial trickster spirit, cast down and held in the frozen north of Icewind Dale.
docs.title: Yin Shen

docs.text: Yin Shen was a lesser god of the celestial heavens — goddess of trickery and mischief, of the kind of trick that is usually harmless. Her family lived under the rule of Tyr , god of justice, though not uniformly: her mother and her sister kept his rule, while her father held that bending a rule was fine so long as nobody got hurt. She was a prodigy of mischief, with an exact sense of which buttons could be pushed and how far. In time she was worshipped for it, by troublemaking children up to no good — and worship made her bolder and her tricks riskier. Her twin sister is Shuāng , a devoted servant of Tyr who defended the celestial realm from the evil spirits that threatened it. The two of them were a matched pair on a battlefield and nearly unbeatable together: Shuāng loud and deliberate in heavy armor, drawing every eye with the Dragon's Glaive ; Yin Shen gone into the shadows and arriving behind the enemy with her black lotus sword , a blade as dark as night and silent as the grave. In her kimono nobody heard her coming, and by the time they did it was already too late. Yin Shen only fought when made to — usually as a punishment. Her other sentences ran to practising languages, studying threats to the realm, cleaning very fragile objects, cataloguing the armoury, writing apologies to the people she had pranked, and being stuck in fox form for a full day. Shuāng generally carried them out. Among the many gods she annoyed, she kept one mortal friend: a paladin named Aronious III , posted to guard her shrine. He was righteous and good and everything she found tiresome about Tyr, and she spent her afternoons needling him, boasting about what she had gotten away with, and trying without success to get him to worship her.
docs.title: Before the Fall

docs.text: Her mistake was small, and then it was not. At a festival — the night merry, the offerings laid out — she set out to inconvenience her sister and the other gods by blessing a child to interfere with the offerings. He asked to be able to cast a higher tier of fire spells. She assumed a fire dancer, or an evocation mage there to entertain, and she did not look any further into it. By the time she noticed, it was far too late. The night turned from merriment to horror. The offerings were destroyed, the festival ruined, most of the crowd injured, and some of them died . It was nobody's fault but hers, and she has never pretended otherwise. The boy was never punished; the townspeople never learned who had caused it. She remembers his face. It was Shuāng who carried word of the disaster to Tyr. The knock came at her door the next day. She stood before the court and pleaded that she had meant no harm, that it was supposed to be harmless, that no one was supposed to be hurt. The gods would not listen — she could bear that. What she could not bear was that her own sister, the one who had put her there, could not look in her direction. Tyr came down to deliver judgement himself, without bothering to hear her side. He stripped her of her title, her kimono, her magic, her immortality, and her sword. He cast her into Auril 's realm of frost and scattered her possessions across Icewind Dale . The last thing she saw was her family crying. Whether from grief at her banishment or from the belief that she was a monster, she does not know, and may never.
docs.title: The Fall

docs.text: Tyr did not destroy what he took from her. He scattered it across Icewind Dale , which means it is out there. Black Lotus Sword — unrecovered Yin Shen's Kimono — unrecovered Recovering them, and reconnecting herself to the Weave, is what she has been doing in the Dale since the day she landed in it.
docs.title: Scattered Regalia

docs.text: She nearly did not survive the first stretch. She was desperate, and by her own account came close to giving up; what carried her through was the kindness of strangers in Ten-Towns. After that she survived on what she is best at — sneaking, stealing, pranks, and cheating. Liar's dice, poker, whatever was being played in the bar. She did not play for money; she knew better than to draw attention by taking people's coin where they would notice. She played for information, for food, for necessities. Her winning streak at the bar in Dougan's Hole was notorious and entirely tolerated, on the grounds that she never asked for money when she won. How she got into those games with no coin to her name is a question she has declined to answer. She was a thief and a scoundrel, and also a friendly face who liked bringing people joy. She told stories about her time in the heavens that nobody believed and everybody enjoyed, and she collected the town's gossip in exchange. It still pains her that when children pray to her for help with some small mischief, she has no blessing left to give them. Source Condensed from the player's own text — see Yin Shen — Player Backstory .
docs.title: The Years in the Dale

docs.text: On the night the Chardalyn Dragon came for Easthaven , Yin Shen found an alley with no one in it and spoke to her sister Shuāng — the one who had brought about her exile — for the first time since the fall. "I know I fucked up in the past. I don't ask much from you, but please, if you can, help these people out." Snow began to fall. In a frozen puddle the face looking back at her was golden and pale and not her own, there for a moment and then gone, and the sigil of Tyr melted itself into the ice. No weapon came. No spell. But she had been heard, and she walked out of that alley carrying something she had not carried in. She was not the only one to see it: elsewhere in the town, Aronious and Hobbins each caught a glimpse of a figure who looked a great deal like her — one in a shiny rock at the front of the militia, one as a shape among the stars. She offered a prayer of thanks to her sister when the dragon was dead.
docs.title: The Prayer in the Alley

docs.text: Claimed Sephek Kaltro 's reforged dagger, which burned cold in her palm but did not harm her. Melted her way out of the Caer's cistern with kitsune fire and freed five prisoners with her. Bargained twenty gold out of Randy Grailden for the map to the black spire. Caught all four falling phials of a potion chest in mid-air, one-handed, at an uncomfortable angle. Shaved, cropped, and re-dyed Dzaan into "Gustavo" so he could walk into Easthaven without burning twice. Held the rope at the burning goblin stronghold until every one of her companions was down it. Pinned the Chardalyn Dragon's head by driving her shortsword into a vent in its neck. Sold the Sunblight treasure to an Easthaven jeweler without telling anyone, and has still not said what the total was.

docs.text: Aronious III — Player Backstory Player-written This is Aronious's player's own text, published as written. The condensed in-world version lives at Aronious III . Aronious, a paladin of the blessed city, belonged to an Order tasked with the divine duty of protecting the Gods. This was due to the bond between a pantheon of multiple gods, who helped the city through blessings and miracles, in exchange for offerings, faith and protection. As a child, Aronious had grown up watching miracles and divine interventions happen time and time again, and could not help but be amazed. The feeling of hope and inspiration that brewed inside him over time turned into solid determination. Determination to protect exactly what has inspired him as a child. After a few years in the order, Aronious became both strong and respected enough to receive a divine task, to protect one of the holy shrines. As a part of the deal with the gods, the city will receive help from the gods in exchange for offerings and worship, which happened at these shrines. Without the shrines, that part of the deal would be broken, and the gods mercy could turn sour. Therefore, dependable paladins were placed at these shrines to ensure the bond between gods and the city stayed true and pure. Thus making the task of protecting these shrines one of the greatest honors a paladin of the order could be given. The shrine Aronious was dispatched to, was somewhat unexpected... In the outskirts of the town, far away from the dense population, was a shrine not too particularly big, and with few offerings to speak of. The little offerings there were to see, looked like children's toys and scrap, such as whoopie cushions, horns, heck even a small rune to give a minor shock during a handshake. All things that are... well, mischievous. That's when he spotted something peeking from behind the shrine. A small creature, resembling a fox, sneering at him before disappearing into the air. Across the following years, Aronious learned the true reason why this post was empty before he took over. Every day was filled with pranks and tricks by the holy being of the shrine, which had driven away the past Paladins stationed there.. Although he had never spoken to the deity of the shrine, it was easy to summarize which deity it belonged to. This was clearly the work of the goddess of mischief, Yin Shen, one of the less popular deities in the pantheon, but nevertheless one to respect. Throughout the remainder of his service, Aronious and Yin Shen grew close, with Aronious making sure to keep her pranks to a manageable level, and making sure she didn't get out of line. Atleast... that's how it used to be, before she was cast out from the pantheon. It all happened so suddenly, one day he was cleaning up after a silly pie-trap that made a little mess, and the next she was just.. gone, without a trace. Desperate, Aronious prayed to the pantheon for answers, for an explenation, for anything. He was met with but one sentence in the language of the divine, spoken directly into his mind... "because we have declared as such, that is all" Aronious fell to the floor... this?... THIS is the words of the gods he had commited himself to for so long? THIS is the divine beings he was inspired by as a child? No, it couldn't be. These.. things, were not what he had worshipped for so long. Just the image he had believed them to be... but no longer. No longer would he commit his life to protect these unjust gods, whom would exile a fellow god without as much as a trace of reason. The goddess he had spent the last few years protecting and befriending no less. He would not allow this. Without hesitation, Aronious left the order, his city, and his now meaningless duty behind. Only two things were clear in his mind. He would find Yin Shen, and bring her back. While also finding himself... and his purpose. Along the way, Aronious discovered a lot... the art of the bow, the druid's and their connection to nature, and uncanny instincts to survive in the wild. After traveling across multiple nations, Aronious found a trail leading towards a land of cold and blizzards. A place where winter had consumed the once green and bright grass that stretched as far as the eye could see. A place called Ten Towns. He had gotten solid tips from a civilian who found themselves zapped during a handshake by a small lightning rune in the hand... classic Yin Shen, it had to be her. Although unused to the harsh winter terrain, he carried on, until he reached the first town he could spot. As he burst through a door to the local tavern, cold and out of breath, he looked around. Some dwarves... some humans... something he could only assume is three goblins in a trench coat. And last but not least, a... a ferret? Drunk inside a mug of beer, clearly as big as the ferret itself, talking to someone.. but that voice talking to the ferret, it was familiar. It was Yin Shen! He rushed over to hug her, before promptly hitting her head, demanding to know what the hell she was doing in a tavern with a drunk-beer-bathing ferret. After briefly catching up, warming up, and.. sobering up for the ferret atleast: The story begins
