docs.text: Hobbins — Player Backstory Player-written This is Hobbins's player's own text, published as written. The condensed in-world version lives at Hobbins . Origin Hobbins was born in Good Mead to the well-known Hobbins family, owners of The Magikal Morgue, a successful magical curiosity shop. Despite the name, the business was perfectly legitimate—if a little unsettling to first-time visitors. The Hobbins family specialized in buying magical items recovered from the frozen wastes, whether salvaged from the remains of unlucky adventurers or sold by the rare survivors who made it back alive. Every item was carefully cataloged, restored when possible, and sold to collectors, travelers, and aspiring adventurers. Her mother, Logely Hobbins, handled the books and negotiations with sharp precision, while her father, Drumly Hobbins, had an uncanny eye for authentic magical relics. Together they built a small fortune, making the Hobbins family one of the more prosperous households in Good Mead. Hobbins grew up surrounded by enchanted trinkets, cursed curiosities, and stories of impossible adventures. She loved all of it, but she also loved the part her parents never quite understood: the thrill of doing the right thing in the most inconvenient, ridiculous way possible. If someone needed help, Hobbins was the sort to sneak out after curfew, steal back a stolen relic, and leave behind a glittering illusion of a goose wearing a crown just to confuse the culprit. Her parents believed adventuring itself was a terrible investment. In their eyes, adventurers were simply future customers—or worse, future inventory. They had spent years watching ambitious heroes throw away promising futures chasing treasure, only to return broke... or not return at all. Magic was valuable. Knowledge was valuable. But risking your life for either was foolish when you could build a comfortable life studying and trading them instead. Recognizing Hobbins' talent for the arcane, they sent her to study at the prestigious magical academies of Waterdeep, believing she would become a respected scholar, enchanter, or merchant capable of expanding the family business far beyond Icewind Dale. The Turn Life in Waterdeep changed Hobbins in ways her parents never expected. For the first time, she was surrounded by ambitious wizards, dangerous experiments, and libraries filled with knowledge no one in Good Mead had ever dreamed of. While she excelled in her studies, she also developed a reputation for harmless—but relentless—mischief. Illusions, disappearing books, enchanted ink, and practical jokes became almost as common as her spellcasting. If a professor was being cruel, Hobbins was likely to "accidentally" ruin their lecture notes. If a classmate was being bullied, she was just as likely to slip them a helpful charm and a perfectly timed distraction. During school breaks, Hobbins became close friends with a dwarf janitor at the academy, and the two spent their time teaching each other things between chores and quiet moments in the halls. From him, Hobbins learned dwarvish, picking up the language little by little whenever school was out on break. The more she learned, the more the quiet life her parents envisioned felt like a cage. Every ancient spell referenced forgotten ruins. Every professor spoke of discoveries waiting beyond civilization. Adventure stopped sounding reckless—it sounded necessary. Not because she wanted glory, but because there were too many people out there who needed help, too many secrets buried under snow, and far too many rules standing in the way of doing what was right. When Hobbins announced she intended to leave Waterdeep and become an adventurer, her parents strongly opposed the idea. They argued that every treasure worth finding eventually found its way into a shop like theirs without risking one's own neck. Why become the frozen corpse when you could buy from the people who survived? Hobbins disagreed. The Wound Hobbins left home on good terms, but not happy ones. Her parents never truly approved of her decision, believing she was throwing away everything they had worked to provide. Every letter from home politely encouraged her to "come to her senses" and return to the family business before Icewind Dale claimed another foolish explorer. Deep down, Hobbins wants to prove that adventure is more than greed or recklessness. She wants to show her family that the knowledge, friendships, and discoveries made beyond the safety of a shop can be just as valuable as anything sitting on a shelf. More than that, she wants to prove that a person can be kind, useful, and wildly inconvenient all at once—that breaking a few rules to help someone is not a flaw, but a feature. Though she would never admit it aloud, every successful expedition feels like another argument in a conversation she's still trying to win. The Drive Hobbins seeks forgotten magic, ancient relics, and knowledge lost beneath the ice—not simply to become powerful, but to prove that true discovery can only come from those willing to leave the safety of home. One day she hopes to return to The Magikal Morgue carrying artifacts no merchant could have purchased because no one else had ever found them. She also refuses to let the harshness of Icewind Dale change who she is. Even in dangerous places, she delights in confusing enemies, teasing allies, and finding absurdly clever ways to help people. If a plan is too orderly, she will probably improve it. If a problem can be solved with a little chaos and a lot of heart, Hobbins is already halfway there. The Tie Logely Hobbins – Mother. Brilliant businesswoman and co-owner of The Magikal Morgue. Loves Hobbins deeply but believes adventuring is an unnecessary gamble. Drumly Hobbins – Father. Expert appraiser of magical relics. Thinks Hobbins is talented enough to become one of the greatest magical merchants in the North—if she survives long enough to realize it. The Magikal Morgue – The Hobbins family's magical shop in Good Mead, known for buying and selling magical items recovered from Icewind Dale's frozen wilderness. The magical academies of Waterdeep – Where Hobbins spent much of her life studying wizardry and becoming notorious for her magical pranks.

From him, Hobbins learned dwarvish, picking up the language little by little whenever school was out on break. The more she learned, the more the quiet life her parents envisioned felt like a cage. Every ancient spell referenced forgotten ruins. Every professor spoke of discoveries waiting beyond civilization. Adventure stopped sounding reckless—it sounded necessary. Not because she wanted glory, but because there were too many people out there who needed help, too many secrets buried under snow, and far too many rules standing in the way of doing what was right. When Hobbins announced she intended to leave Waterdeep and become an adventurer, her parents strongly opposed the idea. They argued that every treasure worth finding eventually found its way into a shop like theirs without risking one's own neck. Why become the frozen corpse when you could buy from the people who survived? Hobbins disagreed. The Wound Hobbins left home on good terms, but not happy ones. Her parents never truly approved of her decision, believing she was throwing away everything they had worked to provide. Every letter from home politely encouraged her to "come to her senses" and return to the family business before Icewind Dale claimed another foolish explorer. Deep down, Hobbins wants to prove that adventure is more than greed or recklessness. She wants to show her family that the knowledge, friendships, and discoveries made beyond the safety of a shop can be just as valuable as anything sitting on a shelf. More than that, she wants to prove that a person can be kind, useful, and wildly inconvenient all at once—that breaking a few rules to help someone is not a flaw, but a feature. Though she would never admit it aloud, every successful expedition feels like another argument in a conversation she's still trying to win. The Drive Hobbins seeks forgotten magic, ancient relics, and knowledge lost beneath the ice—not simply to become powerful, but to prove that true discovery can only come from those willing to leave the safety of home. One day she hopes to return to The Magikal Morgue carrying artifacts no merchant could have purchased because no one else had ever found them. She also refuses to let the harshness of Icewind Dale change who she is. Even in dangerous places, she delights in confusing enemies, teasing allies, and finding absurdly clever ways to help people. If a plan is too orderly, she will probably improve it. If a problem can be solved with a little chaos and a lot of heart, Hobbins is already halfway there. The Tie Logely Hobbins – Mother. Brilliant businesswoman and co-owner of The Magikal Morgue. Loves Hobbins deeply but believes adventuring is an unnecessary gamble. Drumly Hobbins – Father. Expert appraiser of magical relics. Thinks Hobbins is talented enough to become one of the greatest magical merchants in the North—if she survives long enough to realize it. The Magikal Morgue – The Hobbins family's magical shop in Good Mead, known for buying and selling magical items recovered from Icewind Dale's frozen wilderness. The magical academies of Waterdeep – Where Hobbins spent much of her life studying wizardry and becoming notorious for her magical pranks.

docs.text: Yin Shen — Player Backstory Player-written This is Yin Shen's player's own text, published as written. The condensed in-world version lives at Yin Shen . The story of yin shen begins in the celestial heavens, realm of the gods. Tho not a god herself she was a lesser god. Goddess of trickery and mischief. The kind of tricks that are (usually) harmless in nature. She was raised under the rule of tyr, god of justice. Her family followed his rule. (Atleast most of her family) While her sister and her mother followed tyr, her father thought it was ok to “bend” the rules. As long as nothing bad happened and no one was hurt, it didnt matter too much. She even became friends with a mortal. A human named aronious III, a paladin, who was all about righteousness and good, and was everything that she despised about Tyr. But he made good company for fooling around with and talking about gossip. She spent most of her afternoons (when not in the heavens) communing with Aron, constantly trying to get him to worship her. And annoying him, talking about how she got away with annoying the gods. She was a prodigy of mischief, knowing exactly what buttons to push without going too far. And in time, she did get worshipped for it. (Not by Aron) but by the fun troublemaking children who were up to no good. And when she got worshipped, she got bolder, more risky with her tricks. She was a constant nuisance to her sister, but as much as her sister was annoyed with yin shen, she still loved yin shen. And loved how creative she could get with her pranks. Because at the end of the day, they were family, and they always cared for each other. Although a trouble maker, she was a force to be reckoned with on the battlefield. Side by side with her twin, Shuāng, no one could defeat them. Yin Shen leapt into the shadows and attacked enemies from behind with her black lotus sword. A blade as dark as night, and silent like the grave. When she had her special kimono outfit no one was able to hear her coming. And when they did, it was already too late. Her sister alternatively wore very sturdy and loud armor. Drawing the attention of the enemies with her glaive. The dragons glaive, with a purifying flame that coated the blade, no evil spirit could survive its bite. (also used as a good lie detector) as a follower of tyr, Shuāng happily defended the realm from evil spirits that threatened the celestial realm. Yin shen however, only fought when she was forced to, i.e. Punishment for doing one of her pranks. Other such punishments included: practicing her languages, studying potential threats to the realm. Cleaning very fragile objects, cataloging weapons and inventory, being stuck in her fox form for the entire day. And writing apologies to those she pranked. Her sentences were usually carried out by her sister. When not reprimanding yin shen her past times included, writing poetry, practicing her techniques, trying out new kinds of tea, meditating, practising the flute, and occasionally, eating sweets. Yin shen, on the other hand, loved pranking her sister (Shuāng liked her pranks but she would never admit it outloud), sparring with her, practising magic, also playing the flute, and reading gossip from the mortal plane. And then, came her tragic mistake. A small blessing, seeming insignificant. A blessing towards other gods, including tyr and her sister, seizing the opportunity, she gave a blessing to a child to mess with the offerings. It was during a festival, the night was merry, and full of joy, she sought only to inconvenience her sister and the other gods. But the child had other plans, and yin shen was unaware. She didnt look further into the blessing, because what he asked was to be able to cast a higher tier of fire spells. She thought that possibly he was a fire dancer, or an evocation mage trying to entertain. And by the time she noticed, it was far, far too late. The night of merriment and joy turned into a night of horror and terror. Some people died, but most were injured, the festival was ruined and the offerings were destroyed. This was an egregious mistake that was no ones fault but yin shens, and she knew that well. The boy was never punished because the townspeople never found out who caused the tragedy. Yin shen remembers his face and it will forever haunt her. When the knock came at her door the next day, she knew it was not the friendly knock of her sister or a fellow god. It was a death toll for her. She stood before the court and pleaded her case, trying her best to convey that she meant no harm, it was supposed to be harmless, no one was supposed to get hurt or worse die. But the gods wouldnt listen, she could take that. But what killed her was that her sister, her family, couldnt bear to look in her direction. She didnt care about the gods, or what they thought, but she didnt want her sister to think that she was evil. She didnt want her family to think that she had this twisted dark side of her. Tyr himself came down to her, ready to deliver judgement. Without bothering or caring to hear her side, he stripped her of her title, of her special kimono armor, her magic, her immortality, and her sword. He cast yin shen out into aurils realm of frost, and scattered her items across icewind dale. And the last thing she saw was her family crying. Whether they were sad she was banished, or whether it was because they thought she was a monster, she doesnt know. And she might not ever know. In the time following her banishment yin shen struggled, she was desperate, she almost gave up. If not for the kindness of the strangers of ten towns, she surely would have perished. She devoted her time to finding any way to get back home. And if not, to find her possessions that were banished along with her. And to reconnect herself to the weave. She survived in icewindale doing what she does best. Being sneaky, stealing, pranks, and cheating. Whether its liars dice, poker, or any other games that they played in bars. She played not for money, she knew better than to attract attention by taking their money (when they were aware of it) she won information and food, and necessities. Though she was known for her suspicious winning streak in the bar at dougans hole, people werent bothered by it considering that she never asked for money when she won. How she even got into these games without any coin to her name, that, well that shall remain a mystery. And even though she was a thief, a scoundrel, she was also a friendly face that liked to bring joy to others and help them. While she may not be famous in any sense, she was a joy to see when she entered the bar, and always brought a smile to people’s faces. She regaled tales of her time in the heavens, no one really believed her but they enjoyed hearing her stories anyway. And she loved hearing the gossip of the town. Whether it was someone dealing with an unruly customer, someone's wife cheating on their spouse or someone being wronged by their coworker, she loved hearing it. She isnt a god anymore by any means, but she still loved hearing some of the children pray to her, hoping they would succeed in causing mischief and it pained her that she couldnt give them the blessings they asked for.

docs.text: The Ancient White Dragon Dragon An ancient white dragon that roams Icewind Dale and keeps at least one lair out on the Sea of Moving Ice . Still alive. Still angry. First Sighting The party saw it before they knew what they were looking at. In a ravine northeast of Caer-Konig they found the back half of a polar bear taken in a single bite, and then a snowdrift that shifted and fell away in a small avalanche to reveal a massive head and neck. Aronious spotted a saddle half-buried in the snow with a robed figure strapped into it, head slumped, arms hanging limp. They crept past as quietly as they could. On the return journey it had been re-buried by fresh drifts. The Invitation Hobbins reached it by sending on a theory of Yin Shen 's — that white dragons are benevolent creatures who enjoy the company of people. "Don't panic, we are friendly, need help, Ten-Towns in danger, meet at Redwaters, Lupine can vouch, at sundown in two days. Ciao!" The answer came back low and rasping, like stone grinding against stone. "Come to my lair at the Sea of Moving Ice. You'll find a shipwreck I use as one of my homes." Yin Shen's theory was wrong. The Ambush The shipwreck was a hull opened not by rot or weather but by something that had simply decided a wall was an inconvenience, the edges of the breach smooth in a way that suggested size and indifference in equal measure. Inside were a frost troll, a dragon's hoard glimmering under the ice, and four kobolds who confirmed they served it. Asked whether the dragon was friendly toward Ten-Towns, two of them had to sit down. It arrived the way weather arrives — thunderous wingbeats, the crack of ice giving way, a shadow larger than the hull. "Ahh. I smell the tender flesh and hear the panicked heartbeat of the meal that so eagerly delivered itself to me." Blindness Its eyes are filmed over, pale and clouded . It is ancient enough that its sight has largely failed, and it hunts by smell and sound. That is the only reason the party survived. Tinjong rolled a fog cloud through the hold in a single dense surge and called them out to her, and they ran for her cave while the dragon answered its own anger with a blast of breath aimed at the sky — spears of ice coming down like thrown lances in a tight and terrible rain. Outstanding Yin Shen and Mylbor Tarrfak have an agreement to stay in contact: she wants word of this dragon, he wants word of anything worth hunting. It also sits squarely between Easthaven and the northern sea route. When Dzaan suggested Revel's End as the nearest port to Auril's Island , the party pointed out there was a white dragon in the way, and went to Targos for a ship instead.

docs.text: Chardalyn Dragon Construct (destroyed) The crystal machine with a dragon's heart. Xardorok Sunblight 's weapon, built in the forge beneath Sunblight Fortress out of stockpiled chardalyn , and intended to walk a circuit of all ten towns. Hethyl Arkorran died foretelling it: "Hidden away, buried in the mountains, lies a fortress, a villain, a crystal machine with a dragon's heart! O, mighty wings beating and breath like the sun! Bright enough to BURN away the Rime — to burn us all if you do... not... stop..." In the Forge The party saw it chained beneath an opening in the ceiling of the main forge, runic links burning against dark crystal hide, ringed by a circle of chanting Duergar whose voices were locked to the rhythm of the runes. Vast, black, and furious in the particular way of something powerful that has been made to hold still. They broke the circle, but the chains went slack rather than holding. It raised its head, drew breath, and exhaled — not ice, but radiant light , vaporising the nearest constructs in a single sweep. Its wings snapped to full width and it launched itself up through the hole in the ceiling and north over Icewind Dale. The Route A relief map carved from solid stone in the upper fortress showed the plan: Ten-Towns in precise miniature, a channel cut between all ten settlements in a continuous loop, and a dragon figurine on an iron pole that a crank walked around the circuit. It flew the route as drawn — Dougan's Hole , then Goodmead , then Easthaven . Eight hours. The party ran it in a straight line in the same eight hours and got there first. Capabilities Radiant breath that shattered a section of Easthaven's wall and took a part of the vanguard with it, leaving nothing where it had been Tail, claws, and an ice-laden wing buffet that battered the Shield Guardian , Aronious , his reindeer, and the militia line together Chardalyn plating that turned spears, stones, and arrows — most of what the militia threw simply bounced off Weaknesses It arrived wounded. Light seeped from between its plates where the Shield Guardian had hammered it in the forge — radiance leaking out of something built to hold it in — and its flight was visibly unsteady. A militiaman got a spear under one of the plates and pried. It opened, and something bright leaked out. Hobbins 's lightning chromatic orb blew a gaping wound in that flank, and a second widened it until the core was visible behind it: a small black hole, or a dead star . "Everyone try to hit that weak spot I just exposed." Destruction Aronious lashed its helm-like jaw shut with thorn whip and militia hauled on the vines. The next breath had nowhere to go — it went off inside, and the chardalyn around its head cracked. Yin Shen leapt from a rooftop onto its wing, ran up its back, and drove her shortsword into a vent in its neck, pinning the head. Aronious handed the vines off to the militia, drew the giant's bone longbow further than he ever had, and sent an arrow clean through the core. The body began to swell. Hobbins spent her last magic on a thunderwave that drove the blast back into the dragon and away from the militia standing nearest. It shattered into flecks too small to hold its magic, leaving a crater and a missing section of wall. Around eighty of two hundred militia were still standing. There was nothing in the crater but chardalyn fragments.

docs.text: Chwinga Tiny Elemental, Neutral A chwinga is a tiny elemental spirit that lives in plants, rocks, and rivers far from civilization. Those found in cold climates also live in ice and snow. Painfully shy, chwingas prefer to move about unseen. Chwingas resemble 6-inch-tall animated dolls with mask-like faces, spindly limbs, and wild hair. Their appearance is sometimes foreshadowed by gentle breezes, the sweet smell of flowers, dancing fireflies, or snowflakes. They don't have names and cannot speak. Party Interactions The party first saw one in a moonlit glade with Sephek Kaltro 's blade poised above it. They killed him. Dzaan paid them thirty gold to bring him one for study; they danced, sang, and played ring-around-the-rosy in the snow to coax one out, and nothing came. The chwingas came in their own time instead. The Charms On a night watch in the tundra, one jabbed Aronious sharply in the ribs — tiny, bright-eyed, trembling with barely contained delight at its own audacity. When he did not shout or swat at it, it dissolved into a fit of tinkling laughter, and the two of them sat together in the cold for a while. Then it darted behind a rock and came back carrying a snowflake — enormous relative to its small frame, pristine and many-pointed, glimmering faintly with something that was not quite ordinary light. With great ceremony it pressed the charm into his hand, retrieved two more from behind the rock, and set them carefully where Hobbins and Yin Shen would find them in the morning. It looked back at Aronious once — a look that seemed to say that was entirely the plan all along — and disappeared. All three party members carry one. On their sheets the snowflake is recorded as the Charm of the Ice Troll . Old Acquaintances A chwinga lives in Tinjong 's cave out on the Sea of Moving Ice , its face marked with a pattern the party found immediately and inexplicably familiar. The verbeeg extended her little finger as she passed, and the creature reached up and touched it gently — a greeting, old and certain, between two beings who had known each other for some time.

Dzaan paid them thirty gold to bring him one for study; they danced, sang, and played ring-around-the-rosy in the snow to coax one out, and nothing came. The chwingas came in their own time instead.
docs.title: Party Interactions

docs.text: On a night watch in the tundra, one jabbed Aronious sharply in the ribs — tiny, bright-eyed, trembling with barely contained delight at its own audacity. When he did not shout or swat at it, it dissolved into a fit of tinkling laughter, and the two of them sat together in the cold for a while. Then it darted behind a rock and came back carrying a snowflake — enormous relative to its small frame, pristine and many-pointed, glimmering faintly with something that was not quite ordinary light. With great ceremony it pressed the charm into his hand, retrieved two more from behind the rock, and set them carefully where Hobbins and Yin Shen would find them in the morning. It looked back at Aronious once — a look that seemed to say that was entirely the plan all along — and disappeared. All three party members carry one. On their sheets the snowflake is recorded as the Charm of the Ice Troll .
docs.title: The Charms

docs.text: A chwinga lives in Tinjong 's cave out on the Sea of Moving Ice , its face marked with a pattern the party found immediately and inexplicably familiar. The verbeeg extended her little finger as she passed, and the creature reached up and touched it gently — a greeting, old and certain, between two beings who had known each other for some time.
docs.title: Old Acquaintances

docs.text: Duergar Medium Humanoid (Dwarf), Lawful Evil Like other dwarves, duergar were typically thick, stocky figures, though beyond this there were many differences. Both male and female duergar were typically bald, with females also lacking the capacity to grow facial hair. Many were also thinner than their dwarven brethren. Most obvious, however, was their dull gray skin and hair, often matched with an equally stolid expression. Regular dwarves said they had flat heads, possibly as an insult. Because many duergar found on the surface world were criminal exiles, a surface dweller who encountered one of the gray dwarves was likely to notice facial and arm tattoos that marked the duergar as a traitor to his or her people. In Icewind Dale The duergar the party has faced belong to Clan Sunblight , who stockpiled chardalyn across Ten-Towns to build the Chardalyn Dragon . They fight invisible and enlarged, and they do not survive capture.

docs.text: Shield Guardian Construct, Netherese — party companion A ten-foot golem of ancient stone and iron, bound to an amulet that Dzaan 's simulacrum handed over as payment for being made corporeal. Aronious carries the amulet and commands the construct. It has 64 hit points. Recovery The amulet pulsed with direction — a steady tug toward the mountains like a compass needle finding north — and led the party into a ravine in the Spine of the World where goblins had built a settlement. The Guardian hung at the centre of the stronghold from rope and timber like a puppet with its strings cut: massive, still, and waiting. Activating it set off the alarm that burned the stronghold down. In Battle It reads a battlefield with the cold clarity of something that does not feel fear or exhaustion. At the goblin stronghold it stepped between Aronious and a volley without hesitation, absorbing a dozen arrows as though they were rain, then turned its back to the watchmen and spread itself wide as a ten-foot bulwark with Hobbins sheltered in its shadow. When the worgs surged at Polard , a gauntleted hand swept two of them off the ground entirely. Since then: Punched straight through the rotten hull of a shipwreck on the Sea of Moving Ice and hit a frost troll hard enough to send it into the far wall Plugged the narrow entrance hall of Sunblight Fortress as a wall of iron against nine enlarged Duergar Hammered the Chardalyn Dragon in the forge hard enough that light was still leaking from its plates eight hours later — then worked the same flank open at Easthaven with both fists, and got dragged about by the tail for its trouble Came through a wall of the crashed nautiloid and destroyed a flesh golem's midsection in one blow Stored Smites Aronious can store a divine smite in the Guardian and release it later, and has twice done so without mentioning it to anyone — once before the nautiloid, discharged into the flesh golem, and once more at second level before leaving for Targos . Appearance It came out of the goblin stronghold covered head to toe in goblin graffiti. Hobbins refused to leave it that way. The market in Bremen sold them a bottle of Grizwald's Famous Degreaser — tagline It'll remove anything and everything — which the clerk cheerfully admitted was terrible at removing grease but cut through paint as though it had never existed. Too harsh. They put it back. They bought green, pink, purple, and black paint and a set of brushes instead, and set about making the construct look less like a siege weapon and more like something a person might not immediately flee from. Hobbins applied the finishing touch herself: a pink peace symbol, carefully painted across the Guardian's forehead. It helped. Somewhat.

docs.text: Auril Goddess of Winter Night — the Frostmaiden The goddess whose endless Rime holds Icewind Dale in permanent winter. Every town of Ten-Towns makes a sacrifice to Auril , and the kind varies: food, warmth, mead — and in Bryn Shander , Easthaven , and Dougan's Hole , human. She is not a distant power. The party has seen her. Then the temperature dropped sharply. The stars disappeared. The world was sucked into total darkness. Streaking across the sky, barely visible against the black, Auril flew — her form casting terrible magics to keep the Rime continuing relentlessly, without mercy or end. Hobbins hurled magic missile at the flying visage out of pure rage. The darts faltered and faded before reaching her. Auril took no notice. Her Reach Yin Shen fell to the mortal world marked by Auril's endless Rime. Sephek Kaltro , the blue-eyed killer of Ten-Towns, was said to serve some darker purpose beneath the Frostmaiden's will. He melted into snow when he died. Dzaan was burned at the stake in Easthaven as an offering to her. Ravison is a frost druid of Auril who has awakened creatures across Ten-Towns and set them against the people. Her magic guards the ice of the Reghed Glacier , sealing the buried Netherese city of Ythryn . Neither fire nor pick will open it. Her Island Out in the Sea of Moving Ice lies Auril's Island , and at its centre the fortress of Grimskalle . The Codicil of White is kept there — the book Dzaan believes holds an incantation that can split the glacier. The ice mephit Soppo calls it the lady's book . Opposition Not everyone in the Dale is resigned to the Rime. The verbeeg Tinjong , a servant of Sylvanas , drew a hard line: the fight between Ten-Towns and the Duergar is not her concern, but an endless, unnatural winter pressed against the grain of the world itself is — and anything that moves against Auril can count on her when the time comes.

docs.text: Sylvanas God of Nature The power the Dale answers to when it answers at all. Sylvanas is not worshipped in Ten-Towns' temples; the god is met in the open, in the cold, by people who already understand the wild. Known Servants Tinjong , the verbeeg of the Sea of Moving Ice , names herself a servant of Sylvanas plainly. She drew her own line on that basis: Ten-Towns' war with the Duergar is not her concern, but the Rime is, because an endless unnatural winter runs against the grain of the world itself. Aronious came to Sylvanas by a longer road. He had discarded his paladin vows to the pantheon above before he ever reached Bryn Shander , and what found him in the Dale was something older and closer to the ground — a dire wolf godling healed in a cave, a reindeer that did not run when he reached for it, a Chwinga that kept him company through a night watch. In the forge beneath Sunblight Fortress , with Hobbins lying singed and still on the stone, he pressed his hand to her chest and called on Sylvanas — the same force behind the reindeer and the Chwinga and the herd in the snow. Healing energy passed through his palm. She drew a shuddering breath and came back. See Also Godlings and Divine Energy — the awakened beasts of Icewind Dale and how divine energy moves between vessels Lupine , the dire wolf godling

docs.text: Tyr God of Justice The god Yin Shen was raised in devotion to, and the god who cast her out. She was born to a minor god of order and law in Tyr's stern heavenly line. Where the rest of that line carried judgment and discipline, Yin Shen became a patron of tricks, pranks, and joyous laughter — children whispered her name before mischief, trusting that a well-placed jest and a quick hiding place might earn her blessing. Her fall came through folly rather than malice. Setting out to inconvenience her sister Shuāng and the other gods during a festival, she blessed a child who asked to cast a higher tier of fire spells — a fire dancer or an entertainer, she assumed, and she did not look further. The festival ended in flames, the offerings destroyed, most of the crowd injured, and some of them dead. The Judgement She stood before the court and pleaded that she had meant no harm. The gods would not listen. Tyr came down to deliver judgement himself, without bothering to hear her side . He stripped her of her title, her kimono , her magic, her immortality, and her sword . He cast her into Auril 's realm of frost, and scattered her possessions across Icewind Dale . He did not destroy them. They are still out there. The Order That Guarded the Shrines Tyr's reach extends past his own servants. Aronious III belonged to an Order sworn to protect the gods themselves, in a city bound to its pantheon by a bargain of offerings and faith in exchange for blessings. He spent years guarding Yin Shen's shrine and became her friend. When she vanished without a trace and he prayed for an explanation, the pantheon gave him one sentence: "because we have declared as such, that is all" He left the Order that day. The gods' handling of Yin Shen cost them both of their most devoted. The Alley in Easthaven On the night the Chardalyn Dragon came for Easthaven , Yin Shen found an alley with no one in it and spoke to her sister Shuāng for the first time since the fall. "I know I fucked up in the past. I don't ask much from you, but please, if you can, help these people out." Snow began to fall. In a frozen puddle the face looking back at her was golden and pale and not her own, there for a moment and then gone. Then the sigil of Tyr melted itself into the ice . No weapon came. No spell. But she had been heard, and she walked out of that alley carrying something she had not carried in. Aronious and Hobbins each caught a glimpse of a figure who looked a great deal like her — one in a shiny rock at the front of the militia, one as a shape among the stars. When the dragon was dead, she offered a prayer of thanks to her sister.

docs.text: Chardalyn Material A black crystal that holds magic — and holds something else besides. Chardalyn is the substance the entire Duergar conspiracy was built to gather, and the material the Chardalyn Dragon was made from. What It Does to People Prolonged contact causes a kind of necrosis of the mind . Aronious warned Captain Imdra Arlaggath of it directly after the dragon fell, and told her the fragments in the crater should be buried rather than handled. He had evidence. A captured Duergar held in Easthaven had hidden chardalyn shards on his person and drove them into his own flesh in confinement. Whatever demonic force lives in the crystal devoured what remained of his mind. By the time the guards intervened he had become something feral and unrecognizable, and they put him down. The Thefts The Duergar were stockpiling it. The prisoner taken at the Easthaven town hall admitted that much and would say no more — and when Yin Shen leaned in and asked about a mechanical dragon, his eyes darted, sweat beaded, and he hissed through his teeth: "You'll get no more from me." Known thefts and sources: Easthaven town hall — a large black crystal torn from the chest of a demon-headed ship's figurehead in the promenade, leaving black crystalline shards around the cavity and splinters on the floor below. The Easthaven ferry — named in Durth 's letter as a base from which "the search for chardalyn continues." A chardalyn statuette in a hidden closet at Sunblight Fortress , ringed by mind flayer skulls. Hobbins put a crossbow bolt through it without preamble. The Prophecy Hethyl Arkorran saw what it was being gathered for, and died saying so: "Hidden away, buried in the mountains, lies a fortress, a villain, a crystal machine with a dragon's heart! O, mighty wings beating and breath like the sun! Bright enough to BURN away the Rime — to burn us all if you do... not... stop..." Research Yin Shen carries a chardalyn notebook and studied the material whenever there was light to read by. Dzaan 's simulacrum traded everything he knew about chardalyn as part of the price for being made corporeal. When the dragon burst at the walls of Easthaven, it shattered into flecks too small to hold its magic. There was nothing in the crater but fragments.

docs.text: Godlings and Divine Energy Lore Icewind Dale holds a population of awakened beasts — creatures granted intelligence, power, and a domain of their own. They call themselves godlings, and they keep a balance between them. A godling is recognisable by the faint blue glow or blue wisps rising from its form, and by the collar or band many of them wear. The party found a chamber of ancient stone pillars beneath the cliffs of Lac Dinneshere painted floor-to-ceiling with images of beasts — wolves, bears, eagles — uncommonly large and surrounded by smaller kin, each great creature collared and haloed in blue light. How It Works Hobbins researched this properly in the records room at Bremen , in a book called Nature and the Divine : Godlings act as conduits . Should the vessel for divine energy be destroyed, the energy disperses or finds a new host. She came out of it with an idea she has not yet acted on — that divine energy might be deliberately funnelled into Lupine . The same research let her end the standoff on Maer Dualdon without a fight. The awakened plesiosaur believed that if it stopped tormenting Bremen the spell would break and it would become a mindless beast again. Hobbins convinced it that the awakening is permanent — nothing bound it to that place or compelled it to obey. It descended into the water and shot off away from the town. Known Godlings Godling Form Status Lupine Dire wolf Allied with the party; holds a domain in the eastern wilderness Skree Giant bat Corrupted and killed by the party Ursa Polar bear Expanding her domain; unfaced The plesiosaur of Maer Dualdon Plesiosaurus Released; left Bremen waters Awakening as a Weapon Not all awakenings are gifts. Ravison , a frost druid of Auril , has awakened multiple animals across Ten-Towns and set them against the people — the Maer Dualdon plesiosaur was commanded to make Bremen suffer, and it did. The legend of Angajuk , the whale with a wrecked ship on its back, says a frost druid awakened it too, to carry travelers. Boons A godling can grant power deliberately. After the party killed Skree, Lupine rose to his full height, had them hold their weapons aloft, and exhaled frozen air that settled on the steel and wood as ice crystals before fading into them. Both Hobbins and Yin Shen carry the result as Lupine's Boon : +1 to hit, +1 to damage.

docs.text: Ten-Towns The settlements of Icewind Dale Ten independent towns scattered around the three lakes of Icewind Dale . Each has its own Speaker ; no single ruler governs them all. Yin Shen asked after the leader of all Ten-Towns early on and was told plainly that there isn't one. That absence of central authority is the political problem running under the whole of the party's work. Warning Ten-Towns about the Duergar meant warning ten separate people, one at a time, and hoping each moved. The Towns Town Speaker Sacrifice to Auril Bryn Shander Duvessa Shane Human Targos Naerth Maxildanarr Human Easthaven Danneth Waylen Human Termalaine Oarus Masthew Warmth Caer-Konig Torvus Food Caer-Dineval Crannoc Siever Food Bremen Dorbulgruf Shalescar Warmth Goodmead vacant Mead Dougan's Hole Edgra Dermoot Human Lonelywood The Party's Standing The party holds two written authorities, both earned rather than granted: A writ from Torvus deputizing them as agents of Caer-Konig , reporting directly to the town Speaker, signed and sealed with his signet. An endorsement added by Captain Imdra Arlaggath on the same document stating that while not formally deputized, they are working under official business of Captain Imdra and Easthaven . That paper opened the door at Termalaine and got Aronious onto the wall during the dragon's assault. Mobilisation Imdra sent notices to every town speaker and warned it would take time, as not everyone moved as quickly as she did. She was right on both counts. Termalaine mobilised immediately. docs.text: The settlements of Icewind Dale Ten independent towns scattered around the three lakes of Icewind Dale . Each has its own Speaker ; no single ruler governs them all. Yin Shen asked after the leader of all Ten-Towns early on and was told plainly that there isn't one. That absence of central authority is the political problem running under the whole of the party's work. Warning Ten-Towns about the Duergar meant warning ten separate people, one at a time, and hoping each moved.

docs.text: The Netherese Empire Ancient civilization A dead empire of enormous arcane reach, roughly two thousand years gone, whose ruins are scattered under the ice of Icewind Dale . What it left behind is beyond modern understanding — Hobbins , asked to read the runes on a Netherese device, could confirm only that they were ancient Netherese and leave it there. The Black Spire The party's first contact was The Black Spire , a structure of perfectly smooth, deeply black stone jutting twenty feet out of the frozen earth, swallowing the grey light rather than reflecting it, with no snow clinging to its surface. Something had turned the whole thing upside down. Yin Shen gathered texts on the Netherese empire from its overturned shelves, written in hands long dead, and studied them on the road whenever there was light. She still carries a book of Netheril . At the bottom was a functioning Netherese machine — see The Netherese Machine . It made Dzaan 's simulacrum fully corporeal, and turned a detailed minor illusion of a blowgun into a real one. Temporal Stasis An invisible, locked chest found in a ruined bedchamber of the spire held contents in temporal stasis — airtight, watertight, fixed at a constant temperature. The leather-bound book inside crumbled instantly to ash the moment Yin Shen lifted it out, experiencing roughly two thousand years of age in moments. Hobbins kept the chest. She has ridden out at least one radiant catastrophe inside it. Ythryn The prize is Ythryn , a Netherese city buried in the Reghed Glacier . Auril 's magic guards the ice; neither fire nor pick will open it. The Codicil of White holds an incantation that will. Professor Skant , Dzaan's stolen professor orb, is an expert on the Netherese Empire. Recovering it is part of the same contract. The payoff, as Dzaan put it, is the city itself — and whatever magic is still lying around in it.

docs.text: The Rime The endless winter Auril 's unending night over Icewind Dale . The sun does not properly rise. The snow does not stop. Every town of Ten-Towns pays a sacrifice to Auril to survive it, and the kind varies by town — food, warmth, mead, and in three of them, human. The party saw its maintenance first-hand on a caravan north to Caer-Konig : the temperature dropping sharply, the stars going out, the world sucked into total darkness, and Auril herself streaking across the black casting terrible magics to keep it going relentlessly, without mercy or end. What It Costs The Rime is not only cold. It is an economy collapsing in slow motion. "Times is rough with the winter's Rime shuttering travel, trade, and the joy in our hearts. This is all we have left." — Cori , handing over three gold and six silver, the whole of the inn's savings The Rime fights back against those who travel against it. Pushing northeast out of Caer-Konig toward the Duergar stronghold, the wind and snow picked up dramatically and cut visibility to nothing. Who Opposes It Tinjong , verbeeg servant of Sylvanas — an endless, unnatural winter pressed against the grain of the world itself is her concern, and anything that moves against Auril can count on her. Dzaan — his interest in Ythryn runs through the Codicil of White , and the incantation in it that can split Auril's ice. The party — the voyage north to Auril's Island was sold to a Targos captain on exactly this basis: the voyage was meant to end the frost. The Irony The weapon that could have burned the Rime away was in the hands of the people least interested in doing it. "Bright enough to BURN away the Rime — to burn us all if you do... not... stop..." — Hethyl Arkorran The party stopped it. The Rime continues.

docs.text: Clan Sunblight Duergar clan Xardorok Sunblight 's clan, and the engine of the chardalyn conspiracy. Xardorok abandoned a failing realm in the Underdark when the surface offered him grander dreams of conquest, and committed the clan's whole effort to a single weapon: the Chardalyn Dragon , and a route carved in stone that would walk it through all ten towns. Operations The clan ran a distributed theft operation across Ten-Towns before anyone connected the incidents. Caer-Konig — goods, goats, and the magic lantern from The Northern Light , stolen by a thief whose footprints shrank to nothing at the edge of town Easthaven — the chardalyn crystal torn out of the town hall figurehead; later, a base of operations on the Easthaven ferry , named in Durth 's letter Kelvin's Cairn — a stronghold carved into the mountain holding a zombie ogre, the stolen goods, and cells where denizens of Ten-Towns had been transformed into fungal monsters Sunblight Fortress — the seat, in the Spine of the World , and the forge Their signature is invisibility and enlargement : the Easthaven thief was invisible until Yin Shen walked into him, and nine Duergar in the fortress entrance hall enlarged on sight to fill the corridor with grey iron bulk. They also do not survive capture. Of three prisoners taken, one escaped a cell by shrinking under the door, one drove hidden chardalyn shards into his own flesh and had to be put down, and one was killed at Kelvin's Cairn. The Split The clan was never solidly Xardorok's. Grandolpha Muzgardt , his own paramour, spent considerable time working from inside his command structure to pull Duergar loyalties toward herself, intending to withdraw her people back into the Underdark and revive the realm he had abandoned. Her escort walked the party through his forge. Her Duergar took up the chant on the dragon's chains when the chanters died. When the party left, steel was still meeting steel beyond the walls — the sound of a fortress deciding who it belonged to. Nobody stayed to learn how it came out. Known Members Xardorok Sunblight — lord (deceased) Grandolpha Muzgardt — paramour, rival claimant Durth — son, last known at the Easthaven ferry An unnamed son, killed at the Kelvin's Cairn outpost See also Duergar .

docs.text: Gelp Notice Board Agency No one remembers when the first board appeared. That is the part that unsettles people most, when they stop to think about it — which most don't, because the boards are useful, and useful things tend to stop being questioned. One morning a board was simply there, bolted to a post outside the inn at Bryn Shander , and within a week there was one in every town across Ten-Towns. Sturdy. Weatherproofed. Unmarked by any craftsman's seal or merchant's brand. Towners post to them freely. Grievances, praises, warnings, and recommendations appear in a dozen different hands — ink on parchment, charcoal on bark, wax-sealed letters pinned with care. Fetch requests and odd jobs find their way onto the boards alongside adventurer contracts, missing person notices, and the occasional scathing review of a meal that did not meet expectations. Aronious has been known to leave them. After some days, older postings vanish. Not torn down — simply gone, cleanly, as though they were never fixed there. The space fills again. The deeper strangeness is this: a traveler who mutters a complaint about a leaking roof to no one in particular may find their words, precisely recorded and assigned a rating of one star, on the board the following morning. An offhand compliment to a cook, a remark made in passing to a companion — these too have been known to appear, attributed and dated, as though someone were always listening and always taking notes. No one has seen who maintains the boards. No one has caught them being restocked, repaired, or read. Most people in Ten-Towns have simply decided not to look too hard at the question. The boards work. The cold is already enough to worry about.

docs.text: Knights of the Black Sword A group that is holed up in The Caer , not permitting any admittance and showing signs of aggression to those who wish to enter. They answered a polite request for audience with three warning arrows, one of which grazed Aronious . They wear none of Caer-Dineval 's heraldry. The bodies of guards who did are frozen into the walls of the cistern beneath the castle, where the party also found five beaten and shivering servants of the Caer imprisoned. Speaker Crannoc Siever has not been seen. His office was empty. Unresolved The party escaped the Caer and has not returned. Nothing is known about what the Knights of the Black Sword want, who leads them, or what became of Henry Davis , who was clapped in irons as a traitor for letting them in. docs.text: Music Shop Conspiracy Long suspected by the residents of Easthaven to be twin brothers instead of cousins, Finkle Shortfuse and Hansel Wiresnap own a musical instrument enterprise with zero competition in Easthaven. The two shops owned by the gnomes were paid for, renovated, and opened on the same dates. After a chance run-in with The Frozen Three while out shopping for supplies for their next adventure, their whole scheme was threatened. "I always thought Finkle sounded too similar to Hansel to be cousins. But maybe Gnomes is different than you 'n me?" - Rodney Ashton, materials supplier for Easthaven merchants guild. Aronious , Yin Shen , and Hobbins of The Frozen Three were the first to discover the true identity of the owners. Through sheer happenstance Yin Shen was dead set on buying cymbals for an encounter with an Awakened Giant Bat. Had they only chosen to walk a few yards further and skip over Strings and Sundries, the gnomes secret would have still been in tact. As it happens, they didn't skip over Strings and Sundries. After meeting Finkle Shortfuse he directed them to the other shop. Once there the Frozen Three quickly noticed the similarities and could see through the hasty clothes swap. They were able to corner Finkle and he divulged everything. He had opened Strings and Sundries first, but business had been poor. Believing competition would drive customers, he opened a second shop — only to realize that selling different merchandise meant no competition at all. Now he had two failing businesses and no time to run either properly. The charade of being "cousins" was a desperate attempt to make the shops feel like a thriving family enterprise. Developments Below are the updates based on party interactions. Real Ownership The party made their way to Strings and Sundries to check on the gnome shopkeeper. Inside, they found him busily reorganizing inventory, a look of genuine contentment on his face. When pressed for his real name, he grew sheepish and admitted it: Polard Hinscrop . He was embarrassed by it — the name felt distinctly un-gnomish to his ears. New Management The party returned to Easthaven and made their way to Strings and Sundries . A new sign hung on the door: "UNDR NEU MENAGAMENT" — misspelled, but unmistakable. Polard Hinscrop explained with several conspiratorial winks that he had "sold" the shop to his "brother." This way, both shops could operate as a single business, and he no longer needed the two-gnome charade. He added, still winking, that his "brother" was leaving town. Aronious asked about the departure. The gnome explained he was leaving for the south — tired of the cold, homesick, eager to return to warmer lands. Aronious was so saddened by this news that he pleaded with "Finkle" to join the party on their adventures instead. After a long and absurd discussion between Aronious and "Finkle Shortfuse," it was agreed: by the next day, the gnome would be ready to set out with the party. The Empty Shop On the party's return to Easthaven after the business at Kelvin's Cairn, Drums Emporium was closed and locked, with no lights inside. The shelves were empty, dust hung in the air, and the back room door stood askew. Aronious kicked the door down in fear and haste and found nothing — no wood shavings, no metal dust, and the broken trapdoor between the two shops replaced with seamless, newly installed flooring. Strings and Sundries was still lit and still stocked, now run by a tall, slender woman in a red dress who explained she was the new store manager, the gnome owner having stepped back from day-to-day operations. The Dragon The Chardalyn Dragon's radiant breath went straight down Polard 's lane and left nothing standing. He went to his knees in the rubble and wept. Asked whether the shop had been insured, he produced the pamphlet the party had given him, turned to the last page, and showed them the final unchecked box. "I never got it notarized." The Musical Empolardium A week later the plot was twice its old size, Easthaven's thanks for his part in the defense, holding a tent, a sign, a fresh workbench, and no merchandise of any kind. The rebuilt shop is larger than the old one and about half finished, with a hired assistant named Samantha on the counter. The party offered a better name — a pun — and Polard did not need to think about it. "Samantha, we need to change the sign immediately." Asked after his brother one more time, he hesitated, stepped into the back room, and came out in a different shirt as Finkle Shortfuse . Aronious caught the flicker of confusion and accepted the brother anyway. Yin Shen and Hobbins played along. The conspiracy is, by every reasonable measure, still running. Known Members Finkle Shortfuse Hansel Wiresnap Polard Hinscrop Aronious Yin Shen Hobbins

docs.text: The Frozen Three Adventuring company The fellowship at the centre of this account — bound not by destiny, as Professor Blinkfizzle has it, but by circumstance, courage, and a most inconvenient frost. Members Aronious III — a ranger who turned his back on the gods to chase redemption in the snow, and who has since found his way back to an oath by a different road Yin Shen — a kitsune rogue of celestial origin, fallen, exiled, and lately heard by Tyr again Hobbins — a ferret wizard of alarming intellect and no patience whatsoever They came together at The Northlook Inn in Bryn Shander , took Hiln Trollbane 's contract on Sephek Kaltro , and have not stopped since. Two of the three were not strangers. Before her exile, Yin Shen was a goddess with a shrine on the outskirts of a city, and Aronious was the paladin posted to guard it — the only one who did not let her pranks drive him off. He crossed several nations looking for her after the pantheon cast her down and refused to say why, and tracked her to Ten-Towns on a report of a man zapped by a lightning rune hidden in a handshake. He found her in the Northlook with a ferret drinking out of a tankard roughly its own size. He hugged her, then hit her on the head. Companions Polard Hinscrop — gnome instrument merchant, joined at Easthaven ; currently on hiatus from adventuring to rebuild his shop The Shield Guardian — a Netherese construct bound to Aronious's amulet, painted green, pink, purple, and black with a pink peace symbol on its forehead Dzaan — travelled with them as "Gustavo" until he fled a teleportation circle in the snow; now an employer Mylbor Tarrfak — dwarf trophy hunter, answers a sending immediately and enthusiastically Standing The party holds written authority in two towns: a writ from Torvus deputizing them as agents of Caer-Konig , endorsed by Captain Imdra Arlaggath to add that they work under official business of Easthaven . See Ten-Towns . They are also known, since the night of the Chardalyn Dragon, as the ones who killed it — which has proven more useful in a Targos tavern than any amount of sealed wax. docs.text: Adventuring company The fellowship at the centre of this account — bound not by destiny, as Professor Blinkfizzle has it, but by circumstance, courage, and a most inconvenient frost.
docs.title: The Frozen Three

docs.text: Aronious III — a ranger who turned his back on the gods to chase redemption in the snow, and who has since found his way back to an oath by a different road Yin Shen — a kitsune rogue of celestial origin, fallen, exiled, and lately heard by Tyr again Hobbins — a ferret wizard of alarming intellect and no patience whatsoever They came together at The Northlook Inn in Bryn Shander , took Hiln Trollbane 's contract on Sephek Kaltro , and have not stopped since. Two of the three were not strangers. Before her exile, Yin Shen was a goddess with a shrine on the outskirts of a city, and Aronious was the paladin posted to guard it — the only one who did not let her pranks drive him off. He crossed several nations looking for her after the pantheon cast her down and refused to say why, and tracked her to Ten-Towns on a report of a man zapped by a lightning rune hidden in a handshake. He found her in the Northlook with a ferret drinking out of a tankard roughly its own size. He hugged her, then hit her on the head.

docs.text: Torg's Trading Company An independent caravan company that is widely suspected of suspicious shipments. Though most in Ten Town's keep that to themselves since anyone living in the frozen north will do what it takes to survive. Party Interactions The party first came looking for the company at Trail's End Tavern , where the caravan had taken ten rooms — one of them with its window unlatched and fresh footprints in the snow beneath it. A charmed merchant confirmed that Sephek Kaltro was among them, cold in manner and blue in the eye. By the time the party returned from killing him, the company was gone. Sleds, dogs, and all, departed while they were out in the forest. Travel Vouchers Torg's issues travel vouchers redeemable against caravan passage across Ten-Towns. Torvus of Caer-Konig produced one from his pockets for the party, valid for Eastway travel but not servicing Lonelywood or Dougan's Hole. It took some trouble at the caravan office to prove ownership of it, but it has carried them free of charge ever since. Hobbins also carries Torg's journal , recovered along the way.
